reports.title: M5 Qwen3.5-4B low-copy native kernel profile
reports.report_text:
# M5 Qwen3.5-4B low-copy native kernel profile

Two fresh native control/candidate cohorts completed successfully on Apple M5 / 24 GiB. This is a small 4B serving regression experiment, separate from the handover's M4 / six-profile vLLM objective. No vLLM speed ratio is claimed.

## Handoff assessment and hypothesis

The reviewed handoff is `docs/research/MACBOOK_CODEX_HANDOFF.md`. The current WorldSense native build had all optional optimization flags disabled. The handover's ordered vector vision admission explicitly requires 768 hidden / 12 heads / 216 vision tokens, so its selected d52 route does not apply directly to 4B's 1024 / 16-head encoder. Its extended prefill explicitly limits hidden size to 1024; it is not a route to a wider 4B prefill chunk. Extra interleaved/coalesced/exact-half weight copies also have a different memory tradeoff at 4B. Rejected reduced-bit rejection indexes and reordered vision math were not retried.

Hypothesis: existing chunk recurrence and cache-update kernels improve 4B prompt processing without new body-weight layouts or precision changes. The predeclared candidate uses parallel delta split, chunk convolution, chunk delta, direct chunk writes, attention prefix and resident KV in-place. The graph profile remains chunk16, parallel linear attention, 65,536 image pixels and the same 1,536+256 admission for these calls. No prefix/image/answer reuse or speculation. Every image is freshly prepared and encoded.

## Method and gates

Frozen source is based on `50890a5ca`; `source-manifest.json` records consumed source including instrumentation. The instrumented serving return adds generated token IDs and input/prefill/decode phase clocks to both runtimes. It changes no model math or prompt. Existing native binary is the control. Candidate is built separately from the same tracked source with the six flags. Library hashes, actual backend strings, complete outputs and source-manifest digest are in measurements.json. Official checkpoint is Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B revision `851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a`, both shards plus index, as in the prior serving report.

WorldSense and its managed Cantor service were paused for each cohort and restored in a finally block. Runs were sequential: control1, candidate1, candidate2, control2. Each fresh process ran bunny, car, traffic, bunny; the first request is recorded separately and excluded from the three-request warm median. There are two complete control/candidate cohorts, eight full outputs per runtime, six warm calls per runtime. All generated token IDs match pairwise. Companion Qwen3-1.7B had a separate three-prompt exact-token guard.

The predeclared retention screen requires both cohort warm total/TTFT improvements, complete-token equality, and median decode rate no worse than 2%. This is a smoke screen, not the older 28-stage trained numerical validation or proof over arbitrary input. The native Metal matmul reference passed. No resource exclusions or favorable extra cohort were added. Hardware caches were not flushed.

## Results

| Cohort | Warm median total control → candidate | Warm median TTFT control → candidate | Median decoder prefill control → candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 11.210 → 8.659 s | 4.816 → 2.470 s | 2.439 → 1.320 s |
| 2 | 11.587 → 8.664 s | 4.649 → 2.410 s | 2.573 → 1.497 s |

Total improves 22.8% and 25.2%; TTFT improves 48.7% and 48.1%. The isolated decoder-prefill medians improve about 46% and 42%. Input-phase timing includes CPU embedding/preprocessing and vision build/encode; it is not pure vision GPU timing. The bundle does not isolate which flag causes the gain.

First requests retain setup costs: complete individual records are saved. Peak process footprint is about 16.73/16.92 GB control versus 15.81/15.82 GB candidate. Maximum RSS is about 6.68/9.58 GB versus 10.04/10.04 GB, respectively. These different process measures do not justify a general memory-saving claim. Initialization is recorded separately. These are not camera FPS or production queue latency.

## Decision and remaining work

Retain as an explicit, opt-in Mac WorldSense kernel profile (`cmake/MetalWorldSense4B.cmake`), preserving default options and CUDA builds. The 4B and text guards passed, but broader trained layer/state parity, image grids, grouped-head masking, long contexts, failure recovery and labeled event/search quality still need dedicated 4B coverage. Do not claim general numerical equivalence from greedy-output parity. The handover's full M4/vLLM goal remains unmet and was not adopted as this experiment's target.

The isolated source, builds, stderr/time logs and controllers remain in the local chat's work/4b-handover directory. Native kernel code is unchanged; the new source deliverable is the optional build profile and evidence. The main WorldSense model size, precision, serving resolution and portal/tenant configuration are preserved.

## Documentation audit limit

The index builder includes this report. The legacy all-research verifier stops
at its assertion that today's src/entry/metal_main.cpp equals the older vector
integration hash. The hash still matches that file at handover commit 703da10ff;
subsequent serving work intentionally changed the current entry point before
this experiment. That historical check is not weakened or reported as passing.
This does not invalidate the separate actual token comparisons, but the global
documentation verifier is not green for the current serving branch.

## Local deployment

The same source/flags were rebuilt at out/build/garnet-metal-4b-opt. Its native
matmul reference passed, and all four fixture outputs matched the selected
candidate again before installation. The library was copied into the running
WorldSense bin directory with the original retained as
libgarnet.dylib.before-4b-kernels. Cantor/WorldSense were restored. Deployment
hash is in measurements.json. Future staging must use this optional build
profile; rebuilding the old all-flags-OFF parent target can replace it.

reports.title: Further 4B optimization: shared vision weights and fixed body shapes
reports.report_text:
# Further 4B optimization: shared vision weights and fixed body shapes

Two candidates were actually executed on the M5/24 GiB MacBook against the already deployed six-kernel optimized 4B library. The first was rejected; the second passed its two fresh predeclared timing cohorts, complete output checks and additional state/embedding checks. This is a small Garnet-versus-Garnet serving experiment, not an M4/vLLM comparison or a production accuracy benchmark.

## Bottleneck and implementation

Switching camera aspect ratios rebuilt the entire fixed-grid vision graph, reloaded the checkpoint and uploaded unchanged vision weights. New Metal vision graphs can now use the existing native `build_shared` mechanism: checkpoint path/shape/dtype/offset/size/mtime checks remain in force, and graph-owned buffers retain their lifetime after the old graph closes. Graph replacement becomes transactional; a failed construction does not discard the current encoder. Only one completed grid graph remains active. Images, patches and outputs are not cached; every frame is freshly encoded.

The 4B Metal serving default enables `shareVisionWeights`; explicit false remains available. CPU vision's default builder is unchanged through a method hook, and CUDA paths are unchanged. The optional Mac cache profile additionally enables existing body-only fixed-shape decode kernels. It does not specialize the vocabulary head, change checkpoint precision, reduce pixels, shrink contexts, add weight layouts or use another inference engine. Decoder specialization has bounded pipeline caching and an original-route fallback.

## Methods and gates

Frozen control/candidate Python source manifests and actual library hashes are retained. The selected checkpoint is official Qwen3.5-4B revision 851bf6e806efd8d0a36b00ddf55e13ccb7b8cd0a, with both shards and index. Profile: 1,536 input + 256 output admission, prefill16 parallel linear, 65,536 image pixels; output cap180, same compact JSON prompt, three fixture images. Each fresh process evaluates bunny, car, traffic, bunny. First-after-init is separate; warm medians use the other three calls. No hardware cache flush is claimed.

Each attempt uses the predeclared control/candidate/candidate/control order: four separate processes, two contemporary control/candidate cohorts, eight complete outputs per policy (six warm). WorldSense/Cantor are paused during timing and restored. All first/init measurements, individual successful calls and process memory remain in measurements.json. No timing attempt is excluded or repeated favorably. CPU/input phase clocks include graph building, embedding assembly, preparation and vision execution, not pure GPU time.

## Attempt 1 — vision sharing only: rejected

Token outputs matched; warm total improved 9.4% and 8.2%, TTFT31.8% and30.2%. But cohort2 median decode throughput fell from11.5320 to11.2561 tokens/s (2.39%), exceeding the predeclared2% preservation limit. This candidate was not deployed or rescued by an extra unchanged cohort. The experiment does not isolate whether that small change reflects memory/cache effects or runtime variation.

## Attempt 2 — sharing plus body specialization: retained

The second candidate adds existing BODY_SHAPE kernels, selected to address the prior decode-preservation failure. Both fresh cohorts must improve warm median total by at least5%, improve TTFT, retain all complete generated tokens, and keep median decode within2% of control. Actual last-decode counters must show248 specialized body projections and zero misses per request, with no specialized dispatches in control. All those checks passed.

| Cohort | Median total control → candidate | Median TTFT control → candidate | Median decode tokens/s control → candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 11.340 → 9.087s | 4.279 → 2.455s | 11.389 → 12.154 |
| 2 | 10.781 → 8.915s | 3.605 → 2.233s | 11.287 → 12.124 |

This is another17–20% total-latency improvement versus the previously optimized build, with38–43% lower TTFT and7–8% higher median decode rate in these fixtures. Do not multiply this by earlier component or live-workload gains. Vision graph construction with sharing was about15–19ms median in the full serving runs, versus649–1,475ms control. The separate vision-only test measured shared builds about5–7ms. First initialization still loads weights and retains its cost.

## Correctness and recovery checks

- All642,560 FP32 vision embedding values are bitwise identical across three actual grids (12×20,22×14,12×18) and a return to the first grid.
- Shared replacement survives closing its source; a closed source is rejected. A failing replacement (missing extra vision layer) leaves the original graph usable with identical output.
- Modified patch bytes produce changed embeddings, establishing fresh encoding for that test.
- Sixteen complete generated requests per attempt (eight per policy) match token-for-token.
- After a separate car-image request with16 generated tokens and512-token capacity, all state parts across all32 decoder layers match bit-for-bit between control and retained candidate. This is one sampled request, not exhaustive equivalence.
- Three independent Qwen3-1.7B text prompts match complete tokens between libraries.
- Native Metal matmul reference and the 4B config contract pass.

The exact state/value counts and hashes, drivers and source manifests are included. Broader long-context, grid, batch, concurrency, numerical and labeled semantic-quality coverage remain necessary. No numerical tolerances were loosened. The old global research verifier still encounters the documented historical entry-point hash assertion; it is not represented as passing.

## Memory and deployment

Separate maximum RSS and process-footprint values are in measurements.json. Peak footprint is about12.1GB for the sharing candidate versus about15.8GB in the first attempt's control; maximum RSS is about10.0GB for both. These process observations are not unique GPU allocations or a general memory-saving guarantee. Replacement temporarily retains both graph structures while sharing immutable weights.

The BODY_SHAPE library and serving changes are installed locally with the previous optimized library/source retained for rollback. A launchd bootstrap raced asynchronous removal during deployment; it was recovered by loading the service after removal, stopping the temporary package-owned Cantor, and restarting WorldSense against the single launchd Cantor. Final runtime verification is recorded separately. Portal/default tenant and video-only sources are preserved.

The optional profile is cmake/MetalWorldSense4B.cmake. For an existing CMake cache, explicitly set BODY_SHAPE=ON (cache defaults do not override existing OFF entries), then rebuild/stage Garnet. Fresh builds can use the cache initializer. Serving code changes require a Cantor restart. This retained change includes checkpoint-immutable sharing and original-arithmetic specialization; general model correctness is not claimed from this sample.

reports.title: K32 N64 block packed prefill rejected by numerical gate
reports.report_text:
# K32 N64 block packed prefill rejected by numerical gate

Actual Mac controller PID28401 exited0 after72.469517seconds. Both private
FP32 SIMD tile policies fail the original comparison envelope:6 of48 profiles
across75,601,920 FP32 output values. No timing, confirmation or native integration
was admitted. The matched three-model goal remains active and unchanged.

## Hypothesis and control

The earlier four-output interleaved layout makes neighboring output groups
stride across K. This experiment adds a full BF16 copy in N64/K32 blocks,
K-major inside each block, so a threadgroup loads its contiguous2,048 weights.
Policies1/2 use M32/M64, N64,K32,256threads,32-wide SIMD, and FP32 matrix
accumulation. Decode remains original. BF16 words expand exactly by shifting16;
FP32 inputs, checkpoint values, output/input limits and original key-projection
policy remain unchanged. The result scratch reuses input shared storage after
the final K barrier; static scratch sizes are16/24KiB. M64 skips inactive eight-row
accumulator bands with group-uniform conditions.

The control is the accepted d52 context with its original selected MPS, BF16
and key routes. Both sides use the extra weight allocation; setup is outside
any potential GPU timing. This is a private context, not a selected Garnet
library. Pipeline compilation uses the exact accepted defines with fast math
policy inherited unchanged. Original BF16 words including padded zeros are
roundtripped on CPU for every allocated matrix before upload.

## Complete numerical gate

All29 checkpoint-verified matrices run:7text,7coder,15VL (linear layer0 and
full-attention layer3);20 use the new layout. Physical rows are24/44,26/52,
80/160. Each batch/policy runs four original deterministic activation patterns
against FP64 and control. Preserve gamma based on ceil(K/32)+32, FP32 epsilon,
absolute floor1e-7, and control comparison5e-6+5e-5*abs(control). No bound changed.

The worst FP64 ratio is0.075892469 for both original control and candidate,

# Compact-aware independent decode projections

Status: actual initial component completes and passes original numerical checks; no learned group passes the prospective both-batch gain/null screen. No repeat or native integration.
This experiment targets remaining decode gaps: about0.8% text B1 and7.6% coder
B1 in the last repeated matched comparison. No inference speedup is established.

Hypothesis: put independent same-input projections in one dispatch while
retaining current lossless compact weight traffic and64-thread geometry. The
earlier [raw128 fused study](../../20261015/fused-projection-groups/README.md)
was mixed; it retained raw BF16 traffic and128-thread fused groups, with unused
SIMDs for small projections. Its measurements do not select this candidate.

Control: current native compact64 for eligible matrices, raw128 otherwise,
small64 for <=256 outputs. Candidate: a single64-thread dispatch with disjoint
projection ranges and unchanged separate output buffers. Compact projections
call the exact original compact dot-product body; small projections call the
original small body. Raw large projections use the original per-SIMD dot body
with group output stride8 instead of16 to cover every output with two SIMDs.
No split sums, reassociated reduction, SiLU fusion or concatenated weight copy.
The CPU packer checks raw fallback interleaving and every compact reconstructed
BF16 word. Wide exponent blocks retain original raw fallback. Dense special
FP32-key matrices retain their original raw decode route. Compile Metal3.1,
matching the retained native library, with original default arithmetic options.

Scope: actual layer-zero MLP gate/up for all three models; Q/K/V for text and
coder; irregular read-only pairs; B1/B2. These are learned weights with changed
synthetic inputs, not captured full-model activations. Every original output
and padding bit must match control across four input scales including signed
zero, with the original independent FP64 gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 bound.
Any numerical failure stops the candidate; preserve full failure evidence.

Prospective timing design:2s alternating common warmup; ten complete ABBA
rounds, five samples per window, three window warm calls; retain all samples.
Mode2 is the same control pipelines, bindings and geometry null; mode1 is fused.
No frequency, power or thermal-cause claim is inferred from a null comparison.

Prospective selection: consider a learned model/group only when BOTH B1/B2
improve GPU AND wall time by at least3%, its own null GPU AND wall fractions
stay within5%, every original numerical group passes, and one complete unchanged
confirmation passes the same rule. Report all groups, including negative and
irregular results. No blanket fusion policy from one favorable shape. Kernel
compile/packing and allocation costs are outside these component timings and
must be reported; any later native implementation must reuse existing weight
buffers, validate ownership/fallbacks and complete all full-model profiles.
No full-model or matched-vLLM claim follows from component selection.

The launcher requires the current vector-native inference chain to be terminal,
archived and audited before compilation/GPU execution, then verifies a quiet
exclusive interval. This study must not overlap the running numerical or
performance jobs. Do not mutate any source/driver consumed by those jobs.

Local generated shader/harness and expanded Python runner parse successfully.
No compile, actual packing, GPU numerical or performance result is claimed yet.

To preserve the actual retained control, this component rejects an otherwise
interleaved-only matrix with unsupported K alignment or zero compact blocks;
it does not silently substitute raw128 for an interleaved-only native control.
Native integration would still need that fallback. Weight load/packing/buffer
allocation duration and buffer byte counts are emitted separately from timings;
output allocation is not included in that weight setup duration. No RSS saving
is inferred from these logical buffer byte counts.

Queue PID73358 watches the exact live vector continuation PID67688 at
`logs/vector-vision-native-continuation-20261016`. It waits for successful
terminal/archive/audit completion before the quiet guarded launch. It archives
each terminal component success or failure, independently audits success and
applies the prospective selection rule before allowing one unchanged complete
confirmation. No inference/GPU job is launched by queue creation. All seven
new consumed helper files are frozen while the queue is live. No existing
source or driver used by the current numerical job was modified.

Commands (ROOT is `/Users/zsdx/garnet-metal-investigation`):

```text
python3 ROOT/source/test2026/metal/queue_compact_fused_projection_groups.py ROOT ROOT/logs/compact-fused-projection-groups-queue-20261016 67688
```

The controller records the exact expanded compile/run/archive/audit commands
when dispatched. Frozen raw data, numerical gates, complete ABBA windows and
negative outcomes must be retained before any repair or next candidate.

## Dependency resumed after preserved upstream audit-path failure

Original queue73358 exits1 before launching any component: native inference
completed, but its auditor expected a wrong expanded-script filename. The
terminal controller/queue failure is preserved in the vector-native45-file
252aeda0... archive. The repaired audit passes on Mac/Windows without changing
or rerunning the native initial benchmark. Native initial passes its prospective
screen and unchanged confirmation is running under new controller93884.

New queue94685 at `logs/compact-fused-projection-groups-queue-repaired-20261016`
watches exact93884 using new dependency-only wrappers. Original component
runner, shader generator, precision/gain/null gates, cases and sampling are
unchanged. No GPU experiment has yet executed here; all old failure statuses
remain preserved. Repaired helper files freeze while queued.

## Actual initial result: numerical pass, no selection

Component97616 exits0 in51.396588375s. Repaired queue94685 exits0 after
terminal archive, independent Mac raw audit and predeclared decision. Archive
33 files, SHA256:
`28e0d5b2ca20a30347368c47ed88eb7718b4073fd3a2a26dd7509a9f38776548`.
All16 group/batch original output/padding-bit checks and unchanged FP64 bounds
pass;6400 timings remain. All eight groups and all null windows are retained.
Windows artifact/raw audit is pending transfer; no model or vLLM gain follows.

No learned group qualifies in BOTH batches. Text B1 gate/up GPU/wall fractions
1.005035/1.003054, B2 .931431/.954678; coder B1 .969690/.956895 but its
null GPU fraction .913587 fails the5% gate. Coder B2 .925013/.951680 passes

1.001461/.997875, B2 .985406/.993170 misses the3% gain rule. Attention groups

# Three-bit exponent tags plus escapes: descriptive CPU study

Status: actual CPU scan completed and archived; Mac and Windows evidence audits
pass. No packet encoder/GPU kernel/inference implementation or measured speed
gain. No serving change or goal target pass. Do not cite these byte fractions
as inference throughput, GPU traffic or process memory savings.

The retained [coalesced body codec](../../20261015/coalesced-body-block/README.md)
stores four output channels by128 input values:512 sign/mantissa bytes,
256 four-bit exponent-tag bytes, and four metadata bytes. Exponent spans above15
use raw BF16. Hypothesis: replace four exponent bits with three, reserve tag7
for an exact original exponent-byte escape, and preserve every original BF16
bit before unchanged FP32 arithmetic. This differs from changing output grouping,
threadgroup size, FP32 sum order or model precision.

Scan all29 original first-layer fixtures, verify full checkpoint hashes and each
raw checkpoint slice/fixture hash, and apply the retained large-body admission.
Twenty matrices qualify:6 text,3 coder,11 VL. Across129,984 blocks,125,525 have
the retained compact span and4,459 use raw fallback. For each compact block,
choose the seven-exponent window covering most values, with the lowest base
on ties, then record the exact number of escapes. The CPU reconstruction
expression preserves **64,268,800** entries bit-for-bit, including source zeros
and tiny values. This is not a packed-bit-stream roundtrip or GPU numerical test.
It does not describe all transformer layers or vocabulary-head weights.

| Model | Eligible matrices | Blocks | Retained modeled bytes | Ideal fraction | Ranked/aligned fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 6 | 28,672 | 22,389,248 | 0.938683 | 0.985795 |
| Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct | 3 | 25,536 | 19,940,096 | 0.936670 | 0.983627 |
| Qwen3.5-0.8B | 11 | 75,776 | 59,159,808 | 0.938102 | 0.985190 |

Fractions compare hypothetical packet bytes plus unchanged raw fallback data
and metadata, not actual memory transactions. The ideal estimate assumes a
free escape-rank/address lookup:704 tag/sign bytes plus E exponent escapes and
four metadata bytes. The ranked estimate adds32 bytes, one per SIMD lane, and
rounds each candidate payload to16-byte alignment; it retains the original
772-byte packet whenever that is smaller. Both assume four-byte metadata can
also encode the required variable packet addresses; that layout is unimplemented.
Original BF16 masters/raw fallback storage remain available. There is no RSS
or cache-effect measurement, and no CPU packing-cost measurement for a working
packet encoder. GPU lookup/branch/address work remains unknown.

The initial archived CPU fraction denominator omitted four common metadata bytes
for each raw-fallback block. Preserve that report unchanged. The separate
[corrected budget analysis](budget-analysis.json) adds that identical term to
both arms; the table uses the corrected values. Full histograms and original
ratios remain in the [raw report](evidence/logs/compact11-escape-cpu-20261016/report.json).

Decision after this descriptive study: do not select a GPU candidate from these
numbers. Ranked/aligned modeled savings are only1.42% text,1.64% coder,1.48% VL;
the ideal6.1--6.3% assumes unimplemented free lookup. This is a prioritization
decision after seeing CPU results, not a predeclared statistical speed gate or
proof that every possible11-bit implementation loses. No favorable timing
search or inference success is claimed. Revisit only with a concrete lookup
design and unchanged numerical/full-model/repeated-vLLM validation.

The CPU job exits0 in4.830290125s. It ran during native numerical validation,
with no native/vLLM performance cohort admitted during overlap. This CPU wall
time is not an inference benchmark. No Metal, MLX, model loading or inference
runtime is used by the analysis. Source snapshots, Python/NumPy versions,
checkpoint/fixture identities and terminal status are archived. Raw weights
are omitted by size/hash. Both-host auditors recompute byte budgets from the
captured histograms and verify provenance; they do not rerun omitted weights.

Status: local CPU addressing and literal-expression checks pass. No GPU compile,
numerical-equivalence result or performance measurement is established.

prefix across two or four bands while retaining the original per-value float4
recurrence. This could reduce duplicated normalization and barriers, at the
cost of more live registers and potentially lower occupancy. The accepted
kernel already uses a 16-column tile; this is not scalar-to-vector conversion
or the previously rejected extra-dispatch normalization cache.

# Wider delta value tiles GPU component investigation

Status: two complete unchanged GPU cohorts and their fixed selection pass
identical independent Mac/Windows audits. Only width-64 prefill is confirmed.
No native integration or full-model speed improvement is established.

Hypothesis: share the existing Q/K norm prefix and barriers across additional
value bands per group. The original tile is already 16 columns per 128-thread
group. Widths 32/64 retain every original per-value float4 expression while
using more registers. Decode and prefill are separate selections; this does
not reuse the rejected extra-dispatch norm cache.
[Earlier CPU address prerequisite](../delta-value-tiles-addresses/README.md).

## Setup failure and correction

Initial process 92974 exits 1 in 1.358539291 seconds before compilation or GPU
execution: the reused exclusivity guard expects the alias `output`, absent
from the new runner. Freeze all 19 source/metadata/log files before defining
`output=out`. Pre-execution fixture review also catches the original maker's
inactive final token when extending learned cases to chunk 1. Make that token
active for chunk 1 and assert its actual asset values before execution;
longer learned chunks retain an inactive final token. No numerical tolerance
is involved. [Preserved setup failure](setup-failure/archive-verification.json).

The corrected run is separately named `delta-value-tiles-gpu-guardfix-20261016`.
Before launch, require the prior native norm/RoPE cohort and controller to be
terminal and archived, and finish evidence transfers. Use a separate private
tool directory. Freeze its consumed sources until terminal and archived.

## Numerical coverage

preparation, numerical checks and timing. Compile with Apple Clang and Metal;
the standalone control is the original recurrence with only its entry renamed.
Match accepted d52's main-shader default compile options; native-bfloat-body
is disabled. Regenerate shader and fixture-maker transforms independently.

Generate 104 fixtures: 96 synthetic cases across batches 1/2, heads 2/16,
chunks 1/2/16/32/64/80 and ordinary/inactive/correlated/zero-decay modes, plus
8 learned cases at actual first/last linear layers 0/22, batches 1/2 and chunks
1/80. The frozen NumPy maker uses actual trained QKV, convolution, decay and
beta weights with synthetic hidden/prior states. These are component inputs,
not full model requests or learned projections executed by Garnet.

For every case, check padding 0/4 floats, three carried state steps and widths
16/32/64. Change Q each step. Compare output and next-state words bit for bit
against the original kernel; check read-only inputs, inactive outputs, finite
results and state/output padding guards. All 208 profiles/1,872 checks pass.

control self-checks. Native graph/session ownership and full trained-model
validation remain required.

dispatches per command, a 2-second common warmup per width, then own-null
before comparison. Each has 10 ABBA rounds, 3 warm commands and 5 raw timing
samples per window, 6,400 samples total. Keep every raw GPU and wall interval.
Repeated fixture inputs here calibrate the primitive only; full-model request
comparisons prohibit prefix/input/image reuse.

Compute candidate/control ratios of arithmetic means of all 100 raw samples
per policy at each endpoint. Do not normalize by nulls or filter samples.
The runner records endpoint/threshold rules before execution. Mean aggregation
was implemented after launch and before timing values were inspected; this
is not a formal preregistered study.
Require both own-null GPU/wall fractions within [.95,1.05] and both comparison
fractions <=.95 at every one of four endpoints per width/workload. Endpoints
are first/last layer crossed with B1/B2, separately for decode chunk 1 and
prefill chunk 80. Preserve all initial failures through confirmation.

the other three width/workload selections fail. Its component GPU fractions
range .869049–.915350 and wall fractions .876546–.912910. Decode B2 is slower
for both widths; width-32 prefill misses the threshold at layer 22/B1.
These are initial kernel measurements, not TTFT reductions.

source/checkpoint/config identities match. Repeat every numeric case, width,

# Private native width64 recurrent prefill investigation

Status: all 32 fresh native stages and all 72 complete native outputs pass
identical independent Mac/Windows audits. The first native model cohort fails
the predeclared TTFT retention/preservation screen. Reject without confirmation
or promotion; accepted serving source remains d52. No new matched-vLLM target
count is established.

The [two complete component cohorts](../delta-value-tiles-gpu/README.md) select
only width-64 prefill. Copy accepted d52 into a new private tree with 1,410
source files, 12 exact transformations and 4 added helpers. Preserve all
before/after/source identities. The actual Mac preparation matches Windows
regeneration of every transformation and added helper.
[Frozen preparation and prospective gates](preparation.json).

## Native policy and implementation

GARNET_METAL_DELTA_VALUE_TILE64 defaults OFF. Append the confirmed kernel to
the original main shader only under that compile flag. Select only batch 1/2,
chunk 80, 16 heads, key/value dimension 128, aligned FP32 layouts with zero
buffer offsets, and supported 128-thread/32-lane pipelines. Divide the original
16-column group count by four when selecting width 64. Decode and other shapes
retain the original kernel and dispatch geometry.

Reuse the original state-kernel argument, initialized-producer, device,
input/output alias, pending-writer and secondary-output validation. Preserve
original independent output/state allocations and writes; no packed weights,
state-layout changes, numerical approximation or input/prefix/image reuse.
Keep all per-value arithmetic expressions, Q/K normalization and barriers.

Expose real context, graph and resident-session dispatch counters. Reset them
on Begin/Abort, graph/reset/close and session/reset/failure. Capture actual
prefill and every decode step in workers. Agreed text/coder and all decode
requests must report zero selected calls. For VL, count the 18 linear layers
for each actual chunk-80 prefill in the original plan. Original graph/session
trained references assert the selected/fallback counters on every carried step.

and execution, 32 total. Before execution, regenerate/parse the full driver and
independent auditor, preserving checkpoints 25/31/32 and all original numerical
bounds. A local AST-only expansion initially used a dummy source root and could
not find the frozen template; correct only that local preflight path before
deployment. No runtime/driver or bound repair was made.

existing vector primitive also pass. This linked primitive result does not
establish complete native correctness or model performance.

# Three exact half-storage activation planes: prefill feasibility

Status: CPU representation and synthetic MPS probe executed. Finite numeric
checks pass; the three-separate-product strategy is substantially slower.
No learned-model precision/compatibility or inference speed claim.

Motivation: retained-control prefill GPU spans are83.781/144.813ms for VL
B1/B2; text/coder also spend substantial TTFT in prefill. Existing native
common-alpha products use FP32 activations and exact half-stored BF16 weights.
The rejected BF16-feed study rounded source activations. This study instead
asks whether three half-storage pieces can reconstruct source FP32 bits, and
whether the cost of three products leaves useful headroom before decomposition.
This is a feasibility investigation; no algorithmic novelty is claimed.

Represent a bounded normal input by `h0=half(x)`,
`h1=half((x-float(h0))*2^11)`, and
`h2=half((x-float(h0)-float(h1)*2^-11)*2^22)`.
Require finite planes and exact original source-bit recovery; otherwise a future
implementation must retain the original FP32 route. This runtime admission and
fallback are not implemented by the CPU study or the synthetic timing probe.

## Actual CPU representation result

[CPU raw source/plane hashes, cases and versions](cpu-reconstruction.json).
The Windows CPU script exits0 and verifies2,826,240 source inputs over three
model gate input widths, physical rows80/160 and four exact power-of-two scales.
All these bounded synthetic source values reconstruct bit for bit. They are
generated from the same bounded normal bit pattern as the proposed MPS probe,
not captured model activations.

Independently sample255 finite exponent fields, nine selected mantissas and
both signs:4,590 edge inputs. Only769 reconstruct exactly;3,821 require the
original FP32 fallback, including unsupported dynamic ranges/signed-zero cases.
These samples do not estimate real model fallback frequency or universal FP32
coverage. Nothing is clipped or silently rounded into admission.

Final prospective MPS probe source SHA256:
`847f1dc136dcbab13ff537b600ca575e3a7b174fe789bfe692dbc2a2fd01baee`.
The CPU calculation was repeated after adding diagnostic actual-value and
warmup/buffer reporting to that unqueued probe; numeric reconstruction and
all admission counts remain unchanged. No CPU timing benefit is claimed.

```text
python -X utf8 test2026/metal/analyze_half_triplet_reconstruction.py results/20261016/half-triplet-lower-bound/cpu-reconstruction.json
```

## Prospective synthetic MPS lower-bound probe

Use the six actual MLP gate shapes from the frozen model configurations:
inner/output1024/3072 text,896/4864 coder,1024/3584 VL, each with80/160 rows.
Weights are structured nonzero synthetic dyadic values, not learned weights.
Inputs and all three half planes are precomputed on the host, outside timing.
No universal source conversion, learned checkpoint or native inference claim.

Control: one FP32-input/half-weight product, FP32 output. Candidate: three
half-input/half-weight products with alpha1/2^-11/2^-22 and beta0/1/1 into the
same FP32 output. Same-control-pipeline null is a third mode. Dense products
execute through MPSMatrixMultiplication. No claim about MPS internal accumulator
instructions follows from output dtype. Three finite diagnostics distinguish
rounded-half products from observed FP32 products, plus one exact alpha/beta
test requiring all three source pieces to contribute. Any exception or
diagnostic failure stops timing admission and is archived as a negative result.
API reference: [Apple MPSMatrixMultiplication](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metalperformanceshaders/mpsmatrixmultiplication).
The API page/spec fetch did not establish an internal accumulator guarantee;
none is assumed. Earlier explicit Metal mixed-accumulator diagnostics are a
different API and do not prove this MPS route.

For all six shapes/four input scales, require source-bit reconstruction,
complete finite outputs and padding preservation, unchanged independent FP64
gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 AND5e-6+5e-5*abs(reference) envelopes,
and original control-comparison bounds. Numerics precede timing. Conditioning
is2s alternating common warmup; ten complete ABBA rounds, five samples/window,
three window warm calls, both candidate and identical-control null; all records
retained. Capture weight/setup/check duration and logical buffer byte counts
separately. They are not RSS or an inference initialization measurement.

This is an optimistic cost feasibility probe: GPU decomposition, general
exponent handling, native ownership/fallback, trained weights/activations and
full outputs remain unimplemented/unverified. Even a large synthetic gain
cannot establish the full FP32 inference goal or a vLLM comparison. No native
selection or confirmation rule is inferred after inspecting these timings.

Queue PID83151 watches exact compact component controller73358 and requires its
terminal/archive/audit success before quiet guarded dispatch. It archives one
terminal probe success/failure and audits successful raw data; it does not
search for favorable repeats. Existing vector-native jobs stay untouched and
serial. All six consumed helpers are frozen while queued.

```text

```

`logs/mps-half-triplet-lower-bound-queue-repaired-20261016`, watching compact
queue94685. Probe source, diagnostics, source reconstruction and sampling are
unchanged; the CPU evidence still pins847f1dc1.... No failed capability test is
being retried: no capability process has yet launched. All old statuses remain.

## Actual MPS result: numeric feasibility, unfavorable cost

Actual probe98524 exits0 in28.241084708s; queue94813 exits0 after terminal
archive and independent Mac raw audit. Archive20 files, SHA256:
`ee9d69680b18baacb6b1319d91ce1a2cacf4fb86d9f1dd4a160654eaac5383ad`.

diagnostic outputs pass; all six synthetic shape checks,2,826,240 host input-bit

reports.title: Native image preparation, measured through XLang3
reports.report_text:
# Native image preparation, measured through XLang3

The external CPython/NumPy/Pillow image subprocess has been removed from Garnet Metal serving. The replacement is an in-process C++ JPEG/PNG operator exposed as `garnet.prepare_image`, called from the existing XLang3 model-serving script. Learned vision/decoder graphs still execute on native Metal/MPS. This change does not replace XLang3 with another inference engine or claim that all source files cease to use Python syntax.

## Implementation and input contract

Native decoding uses libjpeg-turbo3.2.0 and libpng1.6.59, with EXIF orientation, separable fixed-point bicubic resizing, FP32 normalization and merge/temporal patch layout. It returns a host FP32 tensor directly to the native vision graph, removing the per-frame helper process and patch-file round trip. JPEG warnings indicating damaged input fail closed. Input lengths, dimensions, tensor size, profile and normalization are bounded/validated. Source/error recovery is per invocation.

The initial format contract is JPEG and PNG, including the tested grayscale, CMYK JPEG, alpha/palette PNG,16-bit grayscale PNG and trailing-EXIF cases. Other formats are rejected without a Python fallback; broader formats are follow-up work. JPEG/PNG are native build dependencies, discovered only for the Metal xModel target. The source has a standard-library-only unsupported stub outside Apple Metal, so the CUDA source glob does not acquire JPEG/PNG dependencies. A no-Metal compile/symbol check was executed; a Windows CUDA build was not executed on this Mac.

Native preparation uses strict float compilation without contraction. The runtime's model-specific normalization/geometry comes from official model configs. The older Pillow/NumPy script remains only as an offline reference. The production runtime does not read GARNET_METAL_FRONTEND_PYTHON; that variable was removed from the local Cantor launch agent.

## Quick metrics

Tests are executed by the native XLang3 executable. Offline golden generation uses Pillow/NumPy; it is not a new production dependency. Alternating old-helper/native calls measure five samples per image and include the real old process startup/config/import/file path. Native samples include tensor creation. These component measurements are not VLM inference latency.

| Fixture | Old helper median | Native median |
|---|---:|---:|
| bunny | 284.67ms | 3.69ms |
| car | 275.12ms | 2.12ms |
| traffic | 282.58ms | 5.21ms |

Component wall time is about54–130times lower in these cases. That factor must not be applied to complete inference.

Two fresh control/candidate cohorts use the previously deployed seven-kernel/shared-vision profile as control. Runs are sequential control/candidate/candidate/control, with WorldSense/Cantor paused. Each fresh worker runs bunny, car, traffic, bunny; first-after-init is retained separately, and warm medians use the last three calls. Same model/checkpoint, prompt,1536+256 capacity,180-token cap,65536 image pixels and16-token prefill. Every frame is freshly decoded/encoded. No hardware cache flush or cached answer is claimed.

The predeclared native-port gate requires exact patch/output parity, no external helper in the candidate, and no median total/decode regression beyond5% in either cohort. This architecture-port preservation gate differs from the prior pure-kernel optimization screens and was recorded before timing. It is not proof of a general throughput win.

| Cohort | Median TTFT control → native | Median total control → native | Decode tokens/s control → native |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.369 → 2.108s | 9.450 → 9.457s | 11.550 → 10.989 |
| 2 | 2.307 → 2.093s | 9.358 → 9.201s | 11.564 → 11.357 |

First-token medians improve9–11%; total medians are effectively flat (0.07% slower and1.67% faster). Decode medians are4.86% and1.79% lower, within the declared port-preservation limit, so no decoder-throughput improvement is claimed. First requests include setup variance and are not uniformly faster. Initialization, all individual calls and separate maximum-RSS/process-footprint values are preserved.

## Correctness and integration

Three real video frames have1,173,504 bit-identical FP32 patch values versus the saved reference. Twenty-one synthetic format/orientation/geometry fixtures also match exact patch bits, including EXIF after PNG IDAT. Corrupt/truncated JPEGs and invalid normalization are rejected. The final native test runner is test2026/metal/test_native_image.py, invoked by XLang3 against offline reference manifests.

All eight complete generated outputs per policy match token-for-token in the two timing cohorts. A separate request matches all state parts across32 decoder layers bit-for-bit, and three1.7B text prompts match complete tokens. These are sampled tests, not exhaustive numerical equivalence or semantic accuracy coverage.

The final main-source build additionally passes native matmul and all21 parity fixtures. Serving-API checks accept both a file path and encoded bytes, with the helper environment unset, and produce matching model text with image_preprocess_backend=native-cpp. After deployment, WorldSense has four online file sources and a fresh stored4B observation reports native-cpp. The first live call is a setup/cold sample (~22.9s), not a matched performance comparison. Camera remains unmounted. Existing portal/default tenant remain configured.

The old library/source and launch agent are backed up locally for rollback. The final build is out/build/garnet-metal-native-image. Future staging should rebuild Garnet with the native codec dependencies. The parent build cache retains the same seven optimization flags; chunk32 was not promoted.

## Previous rejected chunk32 attempt

Before the native-port work, extended-backend chunk32 passed full output comparisons and reduced TTFT, but improved total only1–3% and failed a decode-preservation gate in one cohort. It was not deployed. Its separate work/4b-chunk32 selection, clocks and failure decision are retained; no32-layer state pass is claimed because that attempt's validation driver selected the wrong source admission path and stopped. The production profile remains chunk16.

## Limits

This is a local Mac build and small fixture suite. Broader format/color-profile/interlaced/corrupt-image coverage and packaging across hosts remain necessary. Homebrew codec libraries must be available at runtime. No vLLM comparison, general speed ratio, production semantic accuracy guarantee or full native Windows test is claimed. The legacy global research verifier still has its previously documented historical entry-point hash assertion; it was not weakened or reported as passing.

score, exact-greedy, unsafe fallback and ownership checks pass; all six timing
profiles regress. GPU fractions1.393651–1.600489 and wall1.340444–1.563867 reject
confirmation/integration. All six grouped own-nulls are within5%. This is a
private vocabulary-head component; the matched three-model target is unchanged.

## Hypothesis and exact original control

The retained head uses a derived interleaved INT8 row index to reject vocabulary
rows before original BF16/FP32 refinement. Reduce only that index to four signed
bits, halving its payload. Row quantization remains nearest-even with an exact
dyadic scale; the candidate changes its maximum magnitude from127 to7. Keep the
original upward residual/original/reconstructed L2 metadata and strict-math
error allowance, query norm/magnitude guard, exact first1,024-row seed, original
BF16 weights, refinement order and final argmax. This index is used only for
rejection; learned final logits do not use four-bit model weights.

Four output tags fit in a16-bit word; four K terms load8contiguous bytes per lane,
versus16bytes in the retained interleaved index. Signed nibble unpacking recovers
the approximate integer exactly. Every actual CPU-packed integer and padded zero
is roundtripped before upload. The original INT8 control is generated privately
with its unchanged default maximum127 and original shader. Both arms use the
accepted d52 context, identical defines and strict screening compiler options;
the selected serving library is not modified. The component holds both original
weight/index policies concurrently in memory but executes them sequentially.

## Complete original-score and safety checks

All three models finish numeric mode before any timing.51actual captured queries
(17/model:8ordinary B1 steps,8B2 steps and one mixed-row fixture) reexecute the
original full BF16 head and match every frozen GPU score bit. Both screening
policies check every retained score bit and every rejected original score below
the actual exact-seed threshold, plus original greedy token/error flag.102policy
query checks and66zero/tiny/large/NaN/Inf/mixed unsafe checks compare47,488,512
original score values.102ownership cases check pending/foreign writer rejection,
abort counter clearing/unreadability, successful recovery and uninitialized input.

Unsafe rows retain the existing full original refinement. These sampled learned
queries do not certify the inherited screening bounds for arbitrary future
inputs. No numerical tolerance or original predicate was weakened. GPU fixtures
with non-multiple-of-four vocabulary tails, native session/vision/carried-state
validation and full inference remain required before any integration. Windows
CPU preparation covers256signed byte patterns and five padded/irregular layouts;
CPU layout tests are not GPU tail coverage.

## Timings and survivor inflation

Two seconds alternating conditioning precedes step0 at each model/batch. For
each of eight ordinary steps, own-null control/control runs before comparison,
10ABBA rounds per phase,3warm calls/window,5samples/window. All19,200 measured
intervals retained; each grouped side/clock/phase averages800samples over eight
steps, with no filtering, null normalization or selected subset. The mixed-row
fixture is numeric-only. Fractions are candidate/control; above1 is slower.

Pre-execution admission requires both unmet text/coder B1 heads improve GPU and
wall by5%, every group preserve both clocks within2%, and all six grouped
own-nulls stay within5%. A qualifying initial permits one complete unchanged
confirmation; an initial failure stops. Neither confirmation nor integration
is admitted. Grouped nulls are the declared screen; no per-query statistical
significance or population confidence interval is claimed.

Preserve it. This calibration executes 32 dependent normalization pairs in one
command batch, retaining independent outputs for every stage. Each stage
consumes the previous stage's output; the weights and positions of a selected
learned layer remain fixed across the 32 stages. This is a repeated operator
chain, not 32 actual model layers or a request benchmark.

The paired kernel and original arithmetic are unchanged. Use actual learned
native Q/K projection fixtures, checkpoint norm weights, original 32-lane
reductions and precise trigonometry. Compare every stage's output bit for bit
to 32 original pairs. No intermediate output is omitted. Original hidden
fixture preparation is outside the timed chain and identical across policies.

changed-input variants are tested: 232 profiles and 928 cases per cohort.

# Private native paired normalization and RoPE investigation

Status: all 34 fresh native correctness stages and all 72 complete native
outputs pass identical independent Mac/Windows audits. The first native cohort
fails the predeclared TTFT preservation screen. Reject this integration without
a confirmation or promotion; accepted d52 serving source remains unchanged.

After two complete unchanged component cohorts, select only Qwen3-0.6B and
Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B-Instruct matrix rows 1/2. VL and larger rows retain their
original operations. This physical-row rule also covers tiny 1–2-row prefill
chunks; the agreed serving benchmark's prefill shapes remain on the original
path. [Repeated component selection](../paired-norm-rope-chain/README.md).

Freeze a new source tree on accepted d52 vector vision: 1,411 files,
12 transformations and 5 added helpers, preserving every source/before/after
identity. Local regeneration matches the actual Mac preparation exactly.
[Frozen preparation](preparation.json).

The OFF-by-default GARNET_METAL_PAIRED_NORM_ROPE feature recognizes consecutive
Q/K NormRope operations only when they share positions/frequencies and original
normalization/rotary parameters, match a selected geometry, and both outputs
are live. Keep the original per-head arithmetic, independent output allocations,
projections, keys, fallbacks and public writes. Profiling retains isolated
operations. No packed weights, output views, speculative result or model cache.

The graph and resident session expose actual paired dispatch counters. Workers
record prefill and every decode-step count. Serving prefill and VL are expected
to use zero paired calls in the agreed profiles; text/coder decode must report
the actual full-attention layer count. No component ratio predicts model gain.

## Native correctness protocol

Run every original 30 stages afresh, linked paired primitive compile/execution,
and two additional trained text/coder graph/session reference suites, 34 total.
The added suites retain reproducible fixtures at chunks 1/2, both batches and
first/last layers: 16 profiles, 48 carried state steps, 36 selected-row and
12 fallback route checks. Preserve all original hidden/key/value error bounds,
invalid controls, pauses, resets, close behavior and explicit/resident equality.

The generated driver's intermediate counts are 25/31/34 before execution.
Local preflight regenerates the complete runner and independent auditor and
parses every source transformation. No stage-count repair, numerical tolerance
change or reused original validation stage is involved in this native run.

The earlier [process and stage observation](observation.json) records 16 live
stages. Check PID 54126 subsequently exited 0 in 1,898.893526708 seconds,
with all 34 stages passing. The complete independent audits regenerate all
12 source changes and the actual executed driver; no validation stage or
compile stage is reused. [Windows full audit](checks/verification.json),
[identical Mac full audit](checks/mac-verification.json),
[published gate](checks/gate.json).
Current candidate library SHA256:

reports.report_text:
# Exact half inverse CPU verification

The proposed integer inverse reconstructs original FP32 bits from a finite
half word and a scale without a floating conversion and ldexp. Exhaustive
CPU tests pass on Windows MSVC x64 and Apple clang ARM64, including the
Mac CLZ branch. The helper is not installed in a serving runtime and has no
measured setup-time or inference speed benefit yet.

Both hosts execute the same header, SHA256
`2ba0f45baff48f129743b7ee1c54c941ef8a0ec43e58ed686670a8a72882f7c5`,
against the unchanged original EncodeExactScaledHalf codec and an independent
floating reconstruction. Signed zero, finite normal and subnormal half words,
all scales from -64 through 64, nonfinite rejection and invalid-scale output
preservation are required.

| Exhaustive case class | Cases | Exact or admitted | Rejected |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original BF16 codec across 129 scales | 8454144 | 1122816 | 7331328 |
| Half words across 129 scales | 8454144 | 8189952 | 264192 |
| Six invalid scales across all half words | 393216 | 0 | 393216 |

Every admitted original-codec result reconstructs raw BF16 bits shifted left
16 exactly. Every finite half result matches the independent floating inverse;
all rejections leave output unchanged. The invalid scales include INT_MIN,
-1000, -65, 65, 1000 and INT_MAX.

Windows MSVC uses /O2 and /fp:precise. Mac uses /O3, -fno-fast-math and
-ffp-contract=off on the actual M4 with 16 GiB. Invocation, compiler identity,
preprocessor macros, source snapshots, command logs and exhaustive reports are
captured. [Windows audit](windows/verification.json),
[Mac audit](macos/verification.json).

The first Mac compile exited 1 because invoking the resolved clang++ binary
directly did not locate cstdint in this SDK installation. Preserve that failed
attempt before changing the runner to /usr/bin/xcrun clang++. The retry uses
the identical mathematical header and succeeds. This is a toolchain fix;
neither the codec nor numerical acceptance changed.
[Failed compile archive identity](macos-compile-failure/archive-verification.json).

Frozen archive SHA256 values:

- Windows: `f038b2e04bde9c816fba9384543d9aba26df424c908cfdf05fdf4d221a14bc10`.
- Mac failed compile: `0815d96ce7e311d366bce35325166ba8683f0bda2cae2de316afb8ceea2e7a6b`.
- Mac successful retry: `f6adb209df42be096b375d053bc4d205f1247c2f2516544ec3c3c84cc327aa56`.

All three archives are extracted and verified on Windows; the successful Mac
archive is also independently audited on the Mac. These tests establish the
mathematical CPU prerequisite. Learned packing equivalence, setup latency and
any changed GPU or complete-model runtime still require separate evidence.

# Private native text Q/K/V fusion after repeated component selection

Status: rejected after a trained key-cache numerical failure. The accepted
implementation passes the identical saved fixture. No candidate native timing
or promotion was admitted. The historical launch notes below are superseded
by this terminal result; the serving implementation remains unchanged.

## Final rejection

The original driver exited 1 after 25 passing stages because its intermediate
stage-count assertion still expected 23. Preserve that failed run and both
terminal controllers before resuming only the missing stages. The resumed
driver retains the original 25 records, source and library unchanged; six fresh
recovery stages pass. The new trained test then fails at layer 0, batch 2,
chunk 22, physical rows 44, first state step. The suite has 31 passing stages
and an incomplete failing trained stage, not a full 33-stage pass.

| Implementation on identical saved input | Worst original key error bound ratio | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Fused Q/K/V candidate | 1.516545714435 | Fail |
| Accepted d52 control, all three state steps | 0.520408486838 | Pass |

A ratio greater than 1 violates the unchanged bound. The diagnostic verifies
all 21 saved input and expected-buffer identities and uses the original
accepted driver. Both candidate session and graph fusion counters equal 1
on the failing case. Exact packed weight values and FP32 arithmetic did not
ensure acceptable downstream key-cache numerics. This observation does not
identify an internal MPS rounding algorithm.

The failed validation and its stopped controllers are frozen. The rejection
bundle contains 2,195 files, original and resumed failures, reference fixture,
control driver, and successful identical-input diagnostic. Both Mac and Windows
audits pass. Archive SHA256:
`bca55a5986356f6bf6f7c2320d59fb4d71f37f4a40f6b0cb4b027f1a6be6e556`.
[Rejection audit](rejection/verification.json),
[archive identity](rejection/archive-verification.json),
[failed controller identities](count-failure-controllers/archive-verification.json).

The full-QKV performance continuation stopped at the validation failure; no
native model benchmark ran. The next algorithm packs Q/V only and preserves
the original K GPU projection, with separate primitive, learned numerical,
timing and native gates. Full-QKV component measurements cannot establish a
Q/V or model gain.

Selection: two complete unchanged learned component cohorts select only
Qwen3-0.6B. Keep coder excluded despite a favorable repeat after initial failure;
VL is slower. [Complete component evidence](../prepared-union-qkv/README.md).

Copy the retained validated d52 vector-vision source into a fresh private root.

and every before/after/source hash. Build an OFF-by-default feature option
GARNET_METAL_PREPARED_QKV_TEXT. Original independent weights, output allocations,
all three projection writes, FP32 arithmetic and unsupported fallbacks remain.
No activation/input/prefix reuse or speculation. [Frozen preparation](preparation.json).

The graph recognizes only three consecutive projections of the same input,
with exact named q/k/v BF16 weights in the same model.layers attention prefix,
confirmed widths2048/1024/1024 and inner1024. Only physical rows24/44 encode the
prepared route; profiling and unsupported layouts/shapes retain original code.
The context rejects input/output or output/output alias, unready input and
foreign pending writers before encoding any candidate work. All three outputs
remain materialized, so later consumers/public results are preserved.

The resident session has its own GPU context. During session build, prepare
each recognized triple for its supported physical prefill row count on that
session context, using unchanged shared BF16 owners also used by future prefill
graphs. Do not pack lazily during the first encoded frame. Standalone graph.run
prepares on its own context before Begin and includes that cost in its first
execution. Report model setup, first-after-init and warm timings separately;
do not claim preparation is free or hardware caches were flushed. Extra union
payload/scratch are real costs, and preserved original FP32 key caches can have
different first-use allocations. Actual native RSS remains to be measured.

Publish actual graph/session/prefill counters and every decode-step counter.

TTFT by>=3% in two complete unchanged native cohorts, with no profile decode
reduction>2%, all six model/batch profiles and every original output/numerical
gate. Retained d52 vector control library SHA256:
`d52c37e09edf7afb61889037863b1cb338f9ac0b6d98ea62043c3a016af5b55e`.

No native win may be divided by an old vLLM time to claim a fresh target ratio.

compile/execution, and one additional trained random-input text reference stage
(33 total). The new trained stage preserves original dense block bounds and

fixture/expected file by identity for reproduction. Retain invalid-control
rejection, private state, full-output equality, paused/tail, reset and closed
graph controls. No numerical bound is widened.

Actual launcher10766 is confirmed live; configure/build, vector primitive,
QKV compile/primitive, all7 CTests, full vision grids and trained real heads
have exited0. Original exact dense tail cases are executing. This is partial
validation, not a full33 pass. The main/retained libraries stay untouched.

Finalizer15326 watches only10766, verified live. It archives terminal success
or failure, independently regenerates and audits a successful full33 suite,

# Prepared heterogeneous Q/K/V: actual-context GPU investigation

Current final component status: both complete cohorts audited on Mac/Windows;
only Qwen3 text meets the repeated component selection rule. Subsequent private
native validation rejects the full-QKV implementation: it violates the original
trained key-cache bound while the accepted control passes the identical fixture.
This supersedes component admission for native use. No full-model performance
result is established. [Terminal native rejection](../prepared-qkv-native/README.md#final-rejection).

Private generated context only. Accepted vector serving code, independent
weights and original key policies remain unchanged. No model speed claim.

Prepare one exactly packed common-scale half union before Begin. Keep all
three original weights, including current FP32 text/coder key baselines. One
F32-input MPS product writes joined scratch; a Metal scatter copies all Q, K
and V elements into their original independent output allocations. This adds
union weights and output traffic, and may reduce two MPS product encodes; no
internal GPU kernel count or full-model gain is inferred. Preparation and lazy
first GPU use remain separate costs. Original numerical bounds are retained.

## Actual primitive completed

PID6834 exits0 in11.194792416 seconds including quiet interval and compilation.
Twenty-four exact dyadic changed-input cases cover all six physical row counts,
unequal output widths13/5/3, original FP32-key baseline, all three outputs and
joined intermediates. Pending/foreign ownership, alias, abort/recovery,
unsupported profiles, nonexact values and64-group/2-reject bounded strong-owner
controls pass. Original small union payload336 bytes is shared across shapes.
This checks logical outputs, not physical padding or captured model inputs.

Freeze39-file primitive archive SHA256
`11a891b16bb61f63f23fe536437a3ae9eb4750658fb0416cb262744e6d7e42e4`.
Mac audit regenerates the exact context/header and checks source/compile/guard
records and complete primitive output. Windows transfer completes0 before
extraction, and its independent regeneration/audit passes too.
[Both-host primitive audit](primitive/verification.json).

## Learned design, declared before learned GPU execution

First require all58 separate triples, both serving batches and four changed
structured dyadic input patterns (116 profiles/464 changed-input cases).
All56 CPU-admitted triples must use the candidate successfully. VL layers7/23
must reject it and retain unchanged original outputs/counters at both batches.
The18 already combined VL linear-attention layers retain their original route.

Control uses three actual original EncodeBF16MatVec calls with the original
retained_float_key flags. Check each side against independent FP64 dot/sumabs
using gamma(ceil(K/32)+32)*sumabs+1e-7 AND5e-6+5e-5*abs(reference). Compare every
candidate element against the original output with the latter original bound;
scatter output must also equal the joined scratch bits exactly. Changed inputs
are structured synthetic vectors, not captured model activations. No timing
stage is admitted before the complete all-layer numerical/fallback screen.

Before observing any learned GPU results, select first and last CPU-admitted
triples: text layers0/27, coder0/23 and VL3/19, each at both batches. All-layer
numeric coverage still includes the mandatory rejected triples and all interior
groups. Endpoint selection uses CPU eligibility only, not favorable GPU data.
Twelve timed profiles use original-versus-original null, then original-versus-
candidate, each with2 seconds alternating common warmup,10ABBA rounds,3 warm
calls and5 recorded samples/window. Keep every sample. Update inputs and check
complete outputs outside the recorded clocks. Report CPU encode, GPU and
submit/wait wall clocks separately; null is an exclusion gate, not a correction.

A model passes the prospective component screen only if both endpoints at
both batches reduce GPU AND wall means by>=5%, with each own-null fraction in
0.95..1.05 and every numerical/fallback gate passing. Only a complete passing
initial screen admits one unchanged complete confirmation. A repeated component
pass permits private graph work for those models, not a model or overall win.
Graph integration must retain all three outputs, validate live aliases/consumers,
and preserve unsupported fallback before original full native validation and
all-six-profile repeated comparisons. No old-vLLM/new-native ratio or relaxed
precision/output bound may establish the active overall goal.

## Actual all-layer numerical stage passes; timing running

Learned launcher7300 compiles successfully and its complete numeric stage
exits0:116 profiles,464 changed-input cases,188,276,736 independent projection
checks and59,482,112 exact scatter-bit checks. This includes52 original FP32
key matrices and16 required fallback cases for VL layers7/23 at both batches.

process peak RSS323,338,240 bytes, not full-model memory usage.

The fixed first/last CPU-admitted endpoint timing stage is now running after
that complete numerical gate. These observations require terminal archive and
independent raw audits before admission. No model performance claim follows.

Both cohorts retain232 complete learned numerical profiles and9600 timing
samples. Each complete numeric cohort checks188,276,736 projection references

# QV fusion with the original key projection

Final status: reject. All learned component numerical gates pass, including
bit-identical original K outputs, but no model meets the predeclared complete
endpoint timing rule. Do not repeat or integrate this unchanged variant.

Pack Q and V into an exact common-scale half weight matrix, encode one MPS
product, then scatter into the original independent Q/V outputs. K calls the
original EncodeBF16MatVec route. In the retained text/coder configuration,
floatPrefill selects split BF16 key projection with FP32 accumulation; it is
not an FP32-weight MPS projection. The archived factory comment describing an
original K MPS call is imprecise; the actual code calls the original function.
The runtime call and original key output bits are verified.

Keep prior triple eligibility and scale selection conservatively: K still
participates in CPU admission and scale choice, while its original GPU path
and storage remain unchanged. This is not a complete study of every pair
that could be admitted by an independent Q/V scale. All 58 previous triples
are covered; 56 prepare successfully and two retain original fallbacks.

# Separate Q/K/V exact union: full learned CPU eligibility

CPU prerequisite completed and audited on Mac and Windows. No GPU arithmetic,
numerical-envelope, model-latency or decode speed claim follows.

Hypothesis: Garnet lowers separate dense attention Q, K and V projections
consecutively from the same input. Their unequal output widths can share one
prepared exact common-scale half weight buffer and one F32-input MPS product,
followed by a scatter to the three existing outputs. This is a distinct

# Six bit greedy head rejection index rejected by clean timing

## Mechanism and selection provenance

unchanged strict-math screening guard/error allowance. It changes only the
rejection index: final exact seed/refinement use original BF16 weights and
original FP32 arithmetic, with full-logit route preserved.

Four output integers form24bits, and four K terms span three32-bit words loaded
as packed_uint3 (12bytes versus the original16). The shader reconstructs four
24-bit words, extracts six-bit tags and sign-extends exactly. Every CPU-packed
value and padded zero roundtrips before upload. Additional Windows CPU proof,
run after launch, exhausts all2^24 possible word values at each of four positions
with rotated neighboring words:67,108,864 comparisons, plus five padded/irregular
layouts. It does not exhaust all2^96 neighboring combinations or replace GPU
non-multiple-of-four vocabulary-tail tests, which remain unimplemented.

# Streamed decoded body weights component screen

Status: original-bit/FP64/safety checks pass, but the complete six-profile
component screen rejects the candidate. No confirmation, native integration,
serving change or new matched-vLLM target count. Mac and Windows independently
regenerate all sources and produce identical audits and selection.

Hypothesis: consume each reconstructed float4 weight immediately inside its
compact/raw branch rather than retaining four vectors for a later loop. Keep
four outputs per SIMD, 64 threads, original payload/metadata/raw layout, K/j
iteration, accumulation statements and final SIMD reductions. The compiler may
already shorten this lifetime; register count/occupancy is unmeasured.
[Earlier Windows-only source preparation](../streamed-body-weights-preparation/README.md).

## Control and execution

Use a separate private copy of accepted d52's context, not the rejected width64
recurrence library. Both policies use the retained coalesced codec and fixed
64-thread geometry; the candidate selects only the streamed-weight kernel.
Actual context counters verify the original codec in both policies and the new
kernel only in the candidate. Preserve float-key and unsupported fallbacks.
The borrowed harness retains some older raw-BF16/wide/MPS comment/error labels;
the generated context, admission metadata and dispatch assertions establish
this experiment's coalesced control and streamed candidate.

Require the prior native controller to be terminal and archived with its exact
hash, and complete all evidence transfers before launch. Controller 26445 exits
0 in 35.186062542 seconds; runner exits 0 in 35.116723917 seconds. These durations
include setup/compilation/numerical checks/timing and are not inference latency.
No competing inference runtime is admitted. Freeze consumed sources until
terminal archive.

## Complete numeric and timing protocol

Verify all three checkpoints and every original raw BF16 tensor slice before
compilation. Keep all 29 fixture matrices: seven each at text/coder layer 0,
and 15 at VL's first linear layer 0 and first full-attention layer 3. These
include 20 selected matrices: 6 text, 3 coder, 11 VL. Record actual packing
counts. Run every model's numerical
mode before any model's timing mode, with four changed structured activation
patterns and B1/B2. All 24 numerical profiles and 680,832 original FP32 output
values match bit for bit and remain within the original FP64 gamma and comparison
bounds. All 63 tail/fallback/prefill, pending/foreign-writer, abort/recovery and
uninitialized-input safety profiles pass. This is first-layer projection-set
coverage, not all model layers or full requests.

Time each complete projection set in one native submission. At every six
model/batch profiles, use 2 seconds of common warmup, own-null before comparison,
10 ABBA rounds, 3 warm calls and 5 raw timing samples/window. Preserve all 2,400
GPU/wall samples and all routes. Repeated primitive fixtures here calibrate
kernels; full-model comparisons prohibit prefix/input/image reuse.

Before execution, admission metadata requires both unmet B1 text and coder
profiles to gain >=5% on GPU and wall time, all six profiles to preserve both
clocks within 2%, and all own-nulls within 5%. Compute ratios of arithmetic means
of all 100 raw samples per policy/profile. No sample filtering or null
normalization. The analysis implementation follows execution but precedes
inspection of timing values; this is not a formal preregistered study.

All six own-nulls pass. Both unmet B1 profiles miss the 5% requirement, and coder
wall fractions exceed the 1.02 preservation limit at both batches. Do not rescue
the Text B2 or VL observations with a new favorable policy. Reject without a
repeat. Results do not establish that compiler code is identical, only that this
source change fails the fixed measured screen.
[Complete source/numeric/safety/clock audit](initial/verification.json),
[identical Mac audit](initial/mac-verification.json),
[all means and fixed decision](initial/analysis.json),
[identical Mac decision](initial/mac-analysis.json).

## Costs, evidence and reproduction

No new weight layout or logical tensor storage is introduced; a private context
and extra pipeline enable the comparison. Packing, source compilation and setup

# Streamed decoded weight lifetime preparation

Status at the preparation timestamp: Windows-only source preparation and structural preflight. No Metal
compilation, GPU numerical identity, register count, occupancy or speed is
measured. No Mac deployment, native integration or matched-target update.
This saved preparation predates the [subsequent completed GPU experiment](../streamed-body-weights/README.md).

The accepted body kernel reconstructs four float4 weight vectors into an array,
then consumes them in increasing j order. Hypothesis: consume each reconstructed
vector immediately inside its original compact/raw branch, reducing source-level
live weight storage from four vectors to one. The compiler may already optimize
the two source forms identically. This is a candidate to test, not an established
register reduction or speed improvement.

Keep the same four outputs per SIMD, 64 threads, rows 1/2, 128-K groups,
payload/metadata/raw-fallback addresses, bit reconstruction expressions, K and j
iteration order, accumulation statements, final SIMD reductions and writes.
Duplicate the original accumulation loop inside each uniform metadata branch;
only one branch executes. This differs from the earlier two/eight-output,
threadgroup-size and explicit-FMA variants. No new packing, quantization or
activation precision is proposed.

The generated shader reverses to the original text after undoing these explicit
source moves and entry renames. Generate an isolated native context/header with
an actual dispatch counter and original control, plus a draft numeric/safety
harness. The first harness-generation preflight expected three identical policy
loop strings but found two plus a differently named warm loop. Correct only the
occurrence assertion and the separate warm policy bound. No GPU or numerical
acceptance test had executed. [Source preparation record](preparation.json).

A separate prepared probe adds numeric/timing modes. Preserve original exact
output bits, FP64 gamma envelope, finite results and comparison tolerances.
Numerical mode aborts on a failed original gate; a future runner must finish all
three models' numerical runs before any timing mode. Keep original tail,
fallback, prefill, ownership and abort/recovery safety cases, with fixed 64-thread
geometry. The earlier draft harness retains legacy timing text and is not the
proposed calibrated timing protocol.

Prepared timing mode covers all six first-layer projection-set profiles, a
2-second common warmup per profile, own-null before comparison, 10 ABBA rounds,
3 warm calls and 5 raw samples/window. Expected total is 2,400 samples, all
retained. No sample exists yet; the exclusive runner, compiler validation,
independent audit and fixed admission screen must precede a real experiment.
[Separate-mode preparation](calibrated-preparation.json).

Prepared files and their source snapshots are byte-recorded in the
[manifest](manifest.json). This records source provenance only. Actual Metal
compiler scheduling and FP32 contraction can differ despite preserved source
expressions; original GPU output-bit checks remain mandatory. Any future model
comparison must retain full prompts, limits, outputs, numerical gates and the
two-repeat matched-vLLM target.

Preparation ran locally while the private width64 prefill native checks and
controllers consumed frozen Mac sources. Neither that running tree nor its
shared tools were changed by this work. The full 2x decode/half-TTFT goal remains
active.

# Prospective null-first timing design for vector vision
