passed independent Mac/Windows audits and all prospective calibration gates.
The new full candidate cohort PID57747 completed and passed its screen;
unchanged full confirmation PID60693 is running. Original setup/parser
failure remains preserved and excluded. No new candidate or model gain has
been established for trained/full-model inference. Overall goal remains unmet.
The [original initial cohort](../../20261015/vector-vision-context/README.md)
remains rejected: identical-kernel B1 null drifts11.8%, beyond the declared5%.
No old samples are filtered, corrected by a null ratio, or reused as new gains.
No unchanged favorable repeat of the failed cohort is admitted.

Observed old null GPU window means fall from1.58 to0.79ms. Frequency/power
causality was not instrumented. Test a different timing design prospectively:
fixed2s common alternating conditioning per shape (old0.25s), ten ABBA rounds
with five samples per position (old two rounds/twenty). Retain every measured
sample and the original three warm calls per window. These changes reduce
window duration and extend fixed conditioning; they do not guarantee stability.
The scalar/vector shaders, inputs, shapes, four changed-input generations,
output/padding bit checks and original FP64 bounds stay identical.

Before candidate gains: run only variant0, the same scalar pipeline object
and identical geometry in both arms, through all24 original shapes. Require
both GPU and wall null fractions in[0.95,1.05] at BOTH serving batches
(216 keys,12 heads,64 dimensions) in two fresh unchanged null-only cohorts.
Only if the first passes is its one confirmation admitted. A failure stops
this design, with no repeated attempts to find favorable calibration.
No vector candidate executes during those cohorts, though its shader may be
compiled in the shared library. Timing sample count is4800 per null cohort.

Only after both null cohorts pass, admit a new complete three-policy candidate
cohort under this exact design, with all72 original numerical cases. Keep the
old gain rule: all24 cases per vector width pass; at BOTH serving batches,
GPU AND wall fractions<=0.95 with own null within5%. Initial failure stops;
initial qualification admits one unchanged fresh full confirmation. Both must
qualify. If both widths qualify, choose lower geometric-mean serving wall
fraction across both cohorts; exact tie chooses float2. No native/full-model
or vLLM claim follows from synthetic component qualification.

The old cohort is used only to motivate a measurement-design hypothesis,
not to select a vector width. This is a new prospective study, not a repair
of old ratios or a tolerance relaxation. Any native candidate still requires
trained vision, full original validation, complete native output/latency/memory
cohorts and fresh repeated matched vLLM tests before goal completion.


## Preserved parser failure and fresh setup

both exit0. The binary generated all24 original exact-output/FP64 checks and
4800 measured submissions. The Python summary parser still asserted the old
eight windows/twenty samples, while the predeclared new binary generated40
windows/five samples. It stops at that assertion and writes no summary.

`7af5fad7078e3869d313bf12d2725b802d19969d01557feb6415a2f2219ac409`.

Neither policy passes any profile's performance screen; both are rejected without
an unchanged confirmation or native model integration. The null results make
an unstable baseline an insufficient explanation for these large measured
regressions. Instruction scheduling, register use, occupancy and generated GPU
assembly were not measured, so the precise hardware cause remains unknown.
Contiguous BF16 loads and reduced shared scratch alone did not beat the original
selected MPS/BF16 projection sets. Do not rerun unchanged or claim a TTFT benefit.

## Costs and evidence limits

Additional BF16 buffers total88,735,744bytes (84.625MiB) across the three separate
numeric processes, reused for both batches. Upload/preparation totals427.354077ms,
including original preparation, new layout and bit verification. These are
component sums, not full-model storage, added setup latency or peak RSS. Both
measured policies/control carry the same allocations. Transient allocation,

the [prior preparation](../block-packed-prefill/preparation/preparation.json).

The runtime guard checks before/during each executed stage and rejects competing
inference/probes. Both controllers were terminal and archived before moving to
the next run; no consumed runner, generator or context was changed while live.
The numeric/timing runner was frozen before launch. The external verifier was
written separately; a row-identity assertion was added before inspecting clocks
and uploaded into a new separate audit-tool directory. Selection thresholds and
measured source were unchanged. This is not a formal publication preregistration.

# WS-M5-34: cached immutable matrix metadata — resource gate rejected

WS-M5-34: immutable matrix metadata with exact lazy default retirement.
Status: REJECTED at the prospective WorldSense resource feasibility gate.

Hypothesis and prior evidence
The WS15 candidate released 3,036,086,272 bytes of default state inputs and inactive packed outputs, but failed its companion decode preservation gate. WS16 moved autorelease pools to broader graph/session boundaries and also failed. Those rejections remain authoritative. This experiment changes a separate host mechanism: cache immutable matrix layout and storage identities at allocation so alias/layout checks need neither repeated MPS property calls nor per-getter pools. No causal attribution of earlier regressions or expected performance gain is assumed.

Implementation
Seed is the frozen WS15 source, not a promoted rejected prototype. The default-OFF CACHED_MATRIX_METADATA capability requires LAZY_RESIDENT_DEFAULTS. Candidate enables both; control disables both. All remaining settings match the validated WS10 profile. A static source audit finds exactly one MetalMatrix::Impl construction and one matrix assignment, in Allocate. Numeric buffer/device identities and layout/length metadata live inside the owning Impl; no process-global pointer cache or additional strong buffer owner is introduced. Copies share Impl, moves/reassignment replace that owner, and cached identities cannot outlive it. SharesStorage, CompatibleLayout, IsDefaultLayout and MatrixBufferInfo use those immutable values. Every other lifecycle pool, encoding operation, shader, model/runtime source and CUDA file matches the seed. Added C++ correctness diagnostics compare every cached field against live MPS properties outside benchmark timing.

Correctness protocol
OFF/ON and separate fault build native references include actual MPS metadata parity, empty/copy/move/reassignment, independent same/different padded shapes, host update/zero, pending GPU output, Submit/Abort recovery and survival of the allocating context. Existing allocation/alias/release tests remain. Trained four-input recurrence and six-input attention exercise full output/state parity, host/private isolation, inactive rows, malformed controls, ordinary/resident alternation, another private session, shared weights after source close and rebuild. Test-only deferred allocation failure must preserve session/host values and recover exactly. Native API checks compare all finite state bits across 32 VLM and 28 text layers, full generated token IDs, cold/warm prefix behavior and capacity error recovery against the existing accepted references. Native image embeddings and grid/shared-owner changes compare bitwise hashes against previous controls. Native correctness timings are not speed evidence.

Prospective WorldSense protocol
Fresh 8-call resource pair first: identical car frame, Skill, prompt, configuration and golden semantics; at least 10% reduction in sampled Metal allocations and 5% in sampled process physical footprint. Only after a valid resource pass, a fresh 20-call speed pair tests both models' TTFT, total and derived decode rates plus complete native Skill wall against the unchanged 2% preservation limits. Only after that pass, a fresh mirrored four-worker, 48-call full three-frame/query confirmation requires two independently passing pairs. All first/warm calls and failures retained. No favorable unchanged retry, gate relaxation or promotion from component/resource/single-screen results.

Accounting and limits
Allocation-time metadata reads and extra numeric fields belong to initialization costs. Snapshots are not peaks, free RAM or physical GPU residency proof. GPU and host wait spans overlap. Derived decode rate includes host/stop/postloop work; it is not pure kernel throughput. Fixed recorded video frames traverse actual WorldSense Skill/Galaxy/Garnet, excluding live decode, scheduling, event persistence and retrieval/ranking. CPython is orchestration/audits only; image preparation and inference stay native C++/Metal/XLang3. Original BF16 weights, FP32 math, CUDA support, model budgets, images and numerical bounds are preserved. No camera. No competing GPU jobs, builds or archive copying during timing. Restore validated WS10 and four video sources after every cohort.

Final correctness: OFF/ON/fault native tests all 5/5 passed. Trained four-input recurrence and both six-input attention fixtures, ordinary/resident alternation, late second session, invalid controls, close/rebuild and injected second-allocation failure/recovery passed. Full native API checks passed all32VLM/28text finite state bits, generated token IDs, prefix cold/warm and capacity recovery; four image/grid embeddings matched previous controls exactly. Correctness controller61236 exited0 and restarted WS10. All three benchmark analyzers preserve metric, numeric-gate, golden semantic and source-identity AST after replacing only experiment-specific native routing/counter column. Native routing validated against10real correctness calls, rejecting wrong metadata capability and nonzero rehydration. Official Apple storage/property URLs and source immutability audit retained in api-property-evidence.json; no claim of physical residency.

Terminal resource decision: REJECTED. All 8 real WorldSense/Galaxy model calls passed exact outputs, full generated IDs, Skill semantics, input/prompt/config identities, native capability/retirement checks and zero default rehydration. Sampled maximum byte counts and reduction fractions: {"reduction": {"metal_allocated_bytes": 0.1386127060400516, "task_physical_footprint_bytes": -0.0002549932086517437}, "sampled_maximum_bytes": {"candidate-1": {"metal_allocated_bytes": 18867290112, "task_physical_footprint_bytes": 18059327816}, "control-1": {"metal_allocated_bytes": 21903376384, "task_physical_footprint_bytes": 18054723984}}}. Metal allocations fell 13.861270604%; sampled process physical footprint rose 0.025499321%, failing the predeclared minimum5% footprint reduction. These are snapshots, not peaks or proof of physical GPU residency. No fresh speed screen, full confirmation, promotion or favorable unchanged retry. Raw first/followup timings are retained but do not establish speed. Both workers, controller and wrapper exited0. Original WS10 library restored, four video files online, camera unmounted and valid benchmark POST404 verified. Small read-only audits/script preparation occurred during timing; no competing GPU test, build or archive copy.

reports.title: WS-M5-01: fused greedy head through WorldSense — rejected screen
reports.report_text:
# WS-M5-01: fused greedy head through WorldSense — rejected screen

This is an actual WorldSense/XLang3 → Galaxy Garnet-VLM → native Garnet Metal
experiment on the MacBook M5/24 GiB. It is a deployment-specific evaluation of
an existing optional kernel, not a claim of a new fused-head algorithm. The
candidate changes only `GARNET_METAL_FUSED_HEAD_ARGMAX=OFF→ON` relative to the
deployed seven-flag BF16/FP32 Qwen3.5-4B profile. No CUDA/default change,
quantization, reduced image budget, token cap or cached model answer is used.

## Protocol and scope

`protocol.json` records the predeclared screen and machine/base commits;
`cohort-manifest.json` records consumed libraries/serving hashes, process IDs,
system VM/swap and post-run RSS. The four fresh processes run sequentially
control/candidate/candidate/control. There are three immutable archived JPEG
frames from pedestrians, bunny and car videos. Skill cases are an absent
elephant, search-only description, and current-image vehicle presence. The
normal Galaxy filter also calls the 1.7B text reasoner for current-event
verification; a fixed text search-planning request exercises the LLM route.

WorldSense temporarily clears native live Skill bindings during each suite,
restores bindings from the authoritative DB in `finally`, and returns results
without event delivery, WorldState commits or result-store writes. The normal
current-Skill inference and search-planning implementations are reused. This
excludes video decoding, candidate scheduling, temporal memory, deduplication,
event persistence and search retrieval/ranking. The separate live-video
baseline is integration evidence, not matched speed evidence.

Each worker first warms all three frames and the search request, then repeats
the identical sequence twice. All first/warmup calls remain in raw JSON;
only the two later repeats enter the warm medians. There are 18 complete model
calls per worker (72 total), including 12 warm calls per worker. Frame/Skill
hashes, prompt lengths, chunk plans, full generated token IDs and texts are
saved. Each timing worker uses XLang3; a local credential provider and OS
lifecycle controller use CPython, outside inference and measured model calls.
No standalone Garnet inference timing establishes the decision.

The screen requires exact complete outputs, ≥5% 4B decode improvement and ≤2%
median TTFT/total regression in each comparison; the 1.7B route must preserve
decode within 2%. `analyze.py` independently computes these from full records.
No confidence interval, significance, whole-system FPS or general speedup is
claimed. This is a small fixed-case screen, not a publication confirmation.

## Results

| Process | 4B total p50 (s) | 4B TTFT p50 (s) | 4B decode p50 (tokens/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| control-1 | 16.762 | 6.100 | 10.950 |
| candidate-1 | 14.587 | 5.150 | 12.610 |
| candidate-2 | 14.907 | 5.340 | 12.518 |
| control-2 | 14.466 | 5.213 | 12.596 |

All complete token sequences, texts, frame/Skill identities and input counts
match across the four workers. Actual fused decode counters are nonzero only
for the candidate. The apparent first-pair improvement does not survive the
second control: 4B total rises 3.05%, TTFT rises 2.42%, and decode falls 0.62%.
The second 1.7B comparison has 2.69% higher total and 9.58% higher TTFT, despite
1.99% higher estimated decode. The declared gates therefore fail. **Reject
promotion; original deployed profile restored.** No unchanged favorable retry
is used to overturn the result. The control drift is retained, not discarded;
these observations do not isolate its cause or prove the fusion itself caused
all latency differences.

Decode is estimated as `(generated_tokens−1)/(total_seconds−ttft_seconds)`;
the generated EOS prediction may add work, so this is not a hardware-only
kernel rate. Model timings exclude loading, lock queueing, retries and storage.
Native-call and HTTP wall times are separate. GPU/encode/wait counters can
overlap and must not be added as independent costs. Post-run process RSS is
not peak memory or total unified GPU memory; VM/swap snapshots are system-wide.

The first control's warm 4B stage medians are reset 0.018s, host inputs 0.002s,
vision 0.351s, prefill 5.683s, decode 10.469s. These nonadditive medians motivate
a distinct prefill candidate; they do not justify changing the failed head
screen's gates. Telemetry retains token IDs and per-step counters, adding CPU
and diagnostic-storage overhead equally to baseline and candidate.

## Failures and correctness

An initial detached launcher produced no timings and was replaced by an
attached exec session. A native unit test initially misclassified normal
current-image text verification as temporal reasoning; the corrected assertion
requires no temporal reads or state writes. The first HTTP smoke failed to
marshal an unset native `state_changes` value. Initializing an empty list fixes
the transport; the failed response and original logs remain archived. No samples
were returned from that failed smoke; neither repair changed numerical gates.

Native structured-response and state-observability tests pass, including
current-frame admission and serializable no-write state changes. Native
matmul and fused-head bit/FP64/tie/nonfinite/fallback/recovery tests pass at
the original shapes. Extended 2048/2560-width tests are run separately and
their terminal results must be consulted; they cannot retroactively turn this
failed performance screen into an accepted optimization. XLang3 admission
tests reject temporal/geometry cases; unauthenticated benchmark HTTP returns
401. The new recorded benchmark API is opt-in and disabled without the local
`WORLDSENSE_ENABLE_BENCHMARK=1` environment setting.

Raw JSON, lifecycle logs, build/test failures, scripts, base commits, patches
and initial file identities are retained here. Model weights are external
official checkpoints; this archive is not a complete standalone distribution
of WorldSense, video licenses or trained model assets.

The [WorldSense fixed-frame protocol](../worldsense-m5-fused-head/README.md)
is reused in four fresh sequential control/candidate/candidate/control workers:
three fixed recorded-video frames/current or search-only Skills, real Galaxy
VLM perception and text verification, plus fixed text search planning. All
72 complete model-call outputs match, including token sequences, texts and
input identities. Warm metrics use two later repeats of every case; initial
warmup records are retained separately. Live inference bindings are temporarily
cleared, restored in `finally`, and benchmark events/states are not committed.
Video decode, scheduling, temporal states, event persistence and search
retrieval/ranking remain outside this matched timing scope.

Before timing, `protocol.json` requires ≥10% 4B TTFT and ≥5% 4B total
improvement in both comparisons, with 4B/text decode and text TTFT/total
preserved within 2%. The distinct head experiment's failed gates are not
relaxed or reused. No competing GPU probe runs during these timing windows.

| Process | 4B total p50 (s) | 4B TTFT p50 (s) | 4B decode p50 (tokens/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| control-1 | 12.997 | 4.257 | 13.389 |
| candidate-1 | 14.832 | 5.377 | 12.360 |
| candidate-2 | 14.717 | 5.230 | 12.425 |
| control-2 | 14.564 | 5.265 | 12.462 |

First comparison: 4B total rises 14.12%, TTFT rises 26.29%, decode falls
7.68%. Second: total rises 1.05%, TTFT falls only 0.66%, decode falls 0.29%.
Text preservation also fails in the first comparison. **Reject promotion.**
The original library/profile is restored; no unchanged favorable retry is
used to rescue this result. Control drift is retained and its cause is not
isolated. There is no general hardware, model or full-system speed claim.

Actual candidate counters report 1,536 common-alpha dispatches in a
representative 4B prefill, versus zero in control. Thus the policy is active;
the failure is not explained by a completely inactive feature. A header-only
checkpoint size audit, performed during this experiment after its protocol
declaration, finds only **91,750,400 / 7,138,181,120 = 1.285%** of decoder
layer-matrix bytes can pass the existing ≤16 MiB size bound, before exactness
admission. Many large 4B projections remain on the original path. This
documents a scope limitation; it does not causally attribute every regression
to size limits or MPS scheduling.

The candidate retains additional exact-half buffers/row scales alongside
original BF16 decode buffers, adds startup scanning/encoding, and changes MPS
prefill accumulation ordering. It does not quantize learned values. Native
matmul tests include exhaustive integer-codec versus floating-roundtrip
checks, exact-half normal/zero/odd-row fixtures, common-scale cache separation
and unsupported-value fallback. CTest passes. Full WorldSense token parity
passes; the original historical six-profile/19-stage suite is not claimed as
a new M5/4B execution. No model-state bit-equivalence is inferred from text
parity or from exact weight storage.

All raw calls, first/warmup requests, method/gates, builds, libraries/serving
identities, per-cohort stdout/stderr and VM/swap observations are retained.
Model time excludes loading/queues/retries/storage; native and HTTP wall time
are separate. Estimated decode uses `(tokens−1)/(total−TTFT)` and can include

Largest sampled task physical footprint18104565000bytes(16.861GiB), compressed14742028288bytes(13.730GiB). # WS-M5-35: global ownership and OS graphics accounting — diagnostic

WS-M5-35: WorldSense global native ownership and paused OS memory categories.
Status: valid diagnostic; no performance or optimization promotion claim.

Purpose and method
WS34 removed logical Metal allocations but failed the process-footprint gate. This diagnostic distinguishes native owner accounting from OS categories billed to Cantor. Frozen WS34 OFF/ON sources retain the same two policy differences; identical three-file instrumentation adds a many-session inventory API, native request-boundary acknowledgement, and a CPython observer running only vmmap/footprint metadata tools against the verified launchd Cantor PID/birth identity. CPython performs no inference or image preparation. Native execution files, shaders, CUDA and image preparation match WS34. The collection deduplicates graphs and every loaded session together, exposing opaque ordinal buffer IDs and logical allocation sizes/roles without tensor contents. Context/driver scratch may remain outside the collection.

Correctness and identity
Both builds pass all5native reference tests. Trained fixtures verify existing single-session API parity, duplicate graph/session deduplication, two private sessions remaining distinct, invalid object rejection, unchanged host/private states and ordinary/resident lifecycle behavior. Correctness controller93990 exited0. Source, library, models, runtime, SDK, tools, driver and request identities were frozen before dispatch. Eight real WorldSense/Galaxy calls matched WS10 golden full token IDs, text, prompts/configuration, image/Skill identities and interpreted semantics; native retirement/capability checks and zero rehydration passed. Both fresh workers produced4OS captures and exited0; original diagnostic controller96233 exited0. PID/birth checked before every observation. No inference retry or gate change.

Accounting
The installed footprint manual defines Swapped as a subset of Dirty; they must not be added. vmmap separately reports Dirty and Swapped and uses a different view. Native buffer totals overlap OS categories and must not be added to them. Manual/tool identities retained without republishing manuals. Raw OS summaries and native inventories archived for all8boundaries. Pauses, OS inspection and inventory/observer allocations invalidate every timing as speed evidence. Snapshots do not prove exact physical residency of individual buffers or assign a causal performance effect.

Result and next direction
The logical allocation difference after both models ran is exactly3,036,086,272bytes, confined to default-input and legacy packed-output groups. Graphics Dirty accounting is identically17,829,150,720bytes in both workers at each post-companion/warm boundary. Thus this method did not reduce that billed graphics category. Malloc categories are only a few hundred MB, while graphics dominate approximately18GBprocess footprint. Large retained host arrays are not supported as the principal explanation here. Graphics compressed/swapped fractions change across model boundaries and are already included in Dirty; no clock, thermal or compression-caused latency claim.

Next investigate buffers used by live GPU computation, especially scratch/output lifetimes and weights, rather than unused reservations or host malloc trimming. Per-buffer physical/page attribution remains unproven. Existing failed workspace/residency methods remain rejected; no favorable unchanged retry or relaxed gate. No optimization promoted. # WS-M5-25 actual private execution: rejected companion decode regression

WS-M5-25: Actual private execution and dense private output head

Status: REJECTED at fresh speed screen. Correctness/resource pass; companion decode failed the original2%preservation gate. No confirmation, promotion or unchanged retry.

Prior evidence: WS24 exact BF16 vision-master materialization passed correctness and reduced sampled Metal/process allocations14.66%/11.31%, but companion1.7B decode fell26.59%, so WS24 remains rejected. WS23 found warm postbody≤0.000410s and embedding≤0.028945s; it did not support cleanup or embedding as the main cause. WS25 tests execution-policy isolation rather than claiming scope cleanup caused the regression.

Mechanism: defaultOFF Metal PRIVATE_EXECUTION requires DENSE_PRIVATE_STORAGE. Dense decoder layers/prefill graphs already had private storage, but its vocabulary head used ordinary build. New generic build_private preserves ordinary bf16Projections=false and the explicit head bf16_weight operation, then sets the immutable private marker only after successful construction. Dense head uses this method only when the new capability is enabled. Shared construction inherits the marker; failed build, Clear and rebuild reset it.

Native Session.Run accepts alternate graph lists, so policy cannot be cached at Session.Build. The call takes its existing session mutex and sorted distinct actual graph/head locks. It then selects the wholly private path only when every actual participant is ready/private. That path bypasses the reuse StorageScope and empty workspace/retirement bookkeeping. Mixed lists and ordinary heads retain scoped execution. Ordinary Graph.Run selects under its own graph mutex. Helper lambdas retain the same input preparation, GPU commands, exception propagation, Abort, poison/reset, state/output/input behavior and locks. The defaultOFF wrapper retains the old route. Native private/scoped counters increment only after successful calls, reset on Clear/Build, and are cumulative per object; Reset retains them. Serving timings also report private head state. Global-counter overlap test fails as expected before thread_local fix; source/log retained. Final tests/models rerun after fix before timing. Prospective screen uses separate fresh control then candidate processes, one fixed car/currentSkill, first warm plus4measured requests each.20returned model calls; all output/text/tokens/prompt/config/input hashes and0/1native scope counters pass. # WS-M5-17: explicit resident build admission (rejected physical-memory feasibility)

WS-M5-17 explicit resident-build admission — rejected physical-footprint feasibility; no speed promotion.

Mechanism: default-OFF native build_bf16_resident/build_shared_resident admit four-input linear decode and six-input attention/prefill layers. Before lowering, preserve metadata for omitted state inputs1/2; omit only the final returned inactive packed concat root. Allocate live intermediates/outputs/weights normally. Prove three output parts, inactive terminal root, distinct state/output slots, no logical aliases or state writers, valid native geometry/device limits. Preserve normal graph build APIs and ordinary graph.Run materialization after input validation; cache/alias/reset proofs retain same-slot checks when matrices empty. Native counter is requested padded buffer length avoided, not MTLBuffer allocatedSize or physical RAM. Full2048 context, BF16/FP32 arithmetic, CUDA and native C++ image preprocessing preserved. Graph/session lifetime pools retained from WS16.

Development/correctness: first full-model attempt correctly rejects one-input head accidentally routed through resident caller. Fix selects ordinary head construction. Second finds24four-input linear decode graphs still allocating/retiring defaults under six-input-only caller; expand admission to4/6 while preserving zero-retirement requirement. Raw failures and fixes retained. Initial failed-native binary SHA was not captured and early build logs were overwritten; initial sources reconstructable from WS16 seed/prepare.py/recorded fixes, but do not claim exact failed-binary identity. Final measured source/build/model identities are frozen.

OFF/ON6native references pass, including alias/exception/GPU-abort scopes and descriptor-vs-actual-buffer-length/zero/overflow layout tests. Both actual ServeModel/Infer variants match all32VLM/28text finite state hashes/generated tokens, prefix reuse and capacity rejection/recovery against WS10. Trained6-input attention batch1/cap8,batch2/cap64 and4-input linear tests prove initial native buffer inventory omission, ordinary/resident alternation, late second private session, host/private isolation, inactive flags, malformed controls, closure/rebuild. Shared linear graph survives closing original weight source. Separate fault build forces second materialization failure after first succeeds for4/6signatures; private/caller state unchanged and next calls recover exact output. Final serving avoided-storage counters positive, actual retirement and regrowth zero; fault hooks absent from measured binaries.

Prospective staged protocol: first physical-resource feasibility through real WorldSense/Galaxy current-only car Skill. Separate fresh control then candidate; one warmup+one followup each,8model calls retained. Gates: exact outputs/prompts/config/input/hash/Skill semantics/native route, >=10%lower maximum sampled post-decode Metal resources AND >=10%lower maximum sampled task physical footprint. No speed claim from this stage. Only if feasible would fresh4measured speed screens and two independent full3frame/query confirmations follow. Those performance stages were NOT executed.

Result: all8calls exact/native checks pass. Sampled maximum Metal21903376384→18867290112B (−3036086272B/2.828GiB/13.8613%). Maximum task footprint18058983800→18053707192B, difference5276608B (~5.03MiB/0.02922%). Physical10%gate fails. REJECT; no speed validation, promotion or unchanged retry. Initial allocation omission does not demonstrate meaningful physical headroom in this cohort. Sparse/unwritten pages or allocator/driver/VM behavior are hypotheses, not established causes. Task/Metal measures overlap, snapshots not peaks/system free RAM. Every cold/warm/setup/raw timing retained but not a speed result. Fixed-frame scope excludes live decode, event persistence, retrieval and ranking.

Restoration: exact validated WS10 library, normal service without benchmark environment, four file sources online, camera unmounted, authenticated valid benchmark404.

Next distinct mechanism: measured active graph intermediate storage rather than unused defaults. Investigate session-private scratch pools across sequential layer graphs with conservative full native operand liveness and exact-layout interval coloring; protect weights/constants/inputs/output/state/aliases, first-write-before-read proof, strict non-overlap, strong ownership through GPU completion, generic fallback and multiple-session isolation. This is a future design, not implemented evidence in WS17.

# WS-M5-18: active resident scratch pools (rejected physical-memory gate)

WS-M5-18 active resident scratch reuse — rejected physical-resource feasibility; no speed promotion.

Mechanism: session-private standard-layout FP32 workspace pools shared across sequential layer graphs. Conservative native operand liveness (a/b/arguments reads, out/aux writes); protect inputs, outputs/state/storage groups/root, named/held weights, constants and buffer aliases. Admit singleton standard, hazard-tracked resources with one full logical writer before all reads. Exact rows/columns colors reuse only when prior last-read < next first-write. Whitelist MatMul(beta0),BF16MatVec,Norm,Silu,Add,Bias,Mask,Slice,Layout tokenWidth0, and proven scalar/vector full-copy KVChunk. In-place KVUpdate/uncertain partial Conv/Delta operations excluded. Multi-operation fusion configurations rejected. No kernel math/precision/context/image changes or CUDA edits.

Native ownership: session ensures pool capacity before private mutation/GPU Begin; partial growth recoverable. Strong pool owners survive queued GPU work through SubmitAndWait/Abort; graph locks held through completion, bindings cleared on both paths before unlock. Ordinary graph.Run materializes distinct missing scratch/state/root after input validation. Workspace plans reset on graph lifetime/generation. Private sessions own separate pools; caches retain highwater per exact layout until close. Session inventory includes workspace owners; no addresses emitted.

Validation: OFF/ON7native references pass, including strict interval overlap/invalid geometry, queued pending reuse, hazard-tracking property, old-NaN beta0 overwrite, scalar/vector KV copy inactive/tails. Full real serving API32VLM/28text finite state/token/prefix/capacity guards match WS10. Actual buffer counters/pool counts below bound-slot counts and native plan/protected-slot audits validate optimization route. Trained4/6input generic/resident/invalid/inactive/shared-source-close/rebuild/private tests pass; attention second session uses different input and independent reference. Separate-only fault build forces partial pool growth after nonzero state, generic second scratch allocation failure, and layer1 encoder failure after prior layer enqueues/state exchanges. Caller/private allocation-failure isolation, graph inventory unbinding, poisoning/reset and exact recovery pass for4/6two-layer graphs. Fault hooks absent from measured libraries.

Prospective real WorldSense/Galaxy resource feasibility: fresh control then candidate car Skill workers,1warm+1followup each,8model calls. Exact outputs/prompts/config/input/image/Skill hashes, interpreted Skill output, native avoidance/zero regrowth and active workspace route pass. Source/model/build plus external SDK/runtime/toolchain identities frozen before collection. Gates >=10%Metal and >=5%task physical-footprint reduction;5%is~0.9GBof observed18GBtask footprint, a prospective useful-headroom target, not a revision of earlier gates. No timing promotion from resource stage. Speed1warm+4measured and full3frame/query mirrored confirmations were NOT executed after resource gate failure.

Result: maximum post-decodeMetal21903376384→18084315136B, reduction3819061248B(17.43595%). Maximum task footprint18057443728→17285478632B, reduction771965096B(~736.20MiB,4.27505%). Physical5%gate fails. REJECT; no unchanged retry/promotion or speed claim. This is a meaningful observed footprint decrease but below declared acceptance. Metal reduction includes prior unused-default removal plus active scratch changes; do not equate resource counts with RAM or attribute kernel/DRAM/allocator/thermal causality. All first/warm/setup/raw timings retained. Snapshots not peaks/free system RAM; fixed-frame scope excludes live decode/scheduling/event persistence/retrieval/ranking.

Prior-inventory target audit: WS14 other-graph-storage category includes vision buffers, not solely decoder buffers. Large vision shapes [308,4096]/[308,1024]/[308,3072]/[308,4928] total substantial storage; this earlier inventory is prioritization evidence, not a WS18 residual capture/safe-free proof. Current arena deliberately applies only three-output resident layer graphs and leaves ordinary one-output vision execution unchanged. Next distinct scope: conservative ordinary-graph/vision scratch reuse using full operation liveness and separate graph-owned pool. Reuse only already proven full-write operations initially; protect inputs/root/weights/aliases and preserve all ordinary outputs. Design-only here.

Restoration: exact WS10 library, normal service without benchmark environment, four file sources online, camera unmounted, authenticated valid benchmark404.

reports.title: WS-M5-03: immutable shared exact-half body storage — rejected
reports.report_text:
# WS-M5-03: immutable shared exact-half body storage — rejected

This native prototype shares one exact scaled-half allocation between MPS
prefill and strict FP32 decode. It raises the per-matrix admission bound from
16 to 64 MiB, releases the redundant original BF16 allocation for admitted
matrices, and retains the original fallback when exact encoding fails. Normal
half words are converted exactly and corrected by integer FP32 exponent bits;
half subnormals use integer normalization, preserving signed zero. The existing
FP32 dot/reduction order and bounded body specialization remain. Original
learned values are preserved; this is not quantization.

The prototype passed native tests but **failed its WorldSense performance
screen and was not promoted**. More prefill coverage is not itself a useful
whole-model optimization when reconstruction slows generation.

## Declaration, failures and consumed builds

`protocol.json` precedes timing. It requires exact complete outputs, ≥20% 4B
TTFT/≥10% total improvement, decode preservation within 5% on either model,
and text TTFT/total preservation within 5%. These architecture-tradeoff limits
are distinct from the earlier rejected head and limited-half screens. Extra
integer instructions, startup packing and implementation complexity are
declared costs. No standalone inference timing supports the decision.

The first source copy omitted the unchanged nlohmann header; its failed
compile is preserved before dependency repair. Before timing, the normal-value
conversion was refined from an integer-only inverse to an exact normal-half
conversion plus integer exponent correction. Both variants pass exhaustive
GPU correctness checks. No isolated performance probe selected between them.

A first native-service attempt stalled opening the isolated serving source
under Documents, before any model allocation or candidate samples. The process
sample shows the import filesystem-open stack; macOS folder authorization is
suspected, not proven as the sole cause. The attempt's completed control,
logs and consumed library are retained in `documents-root-attempt/`. Identical
sources were packaged under `CantorAI/out/research`; both control and candidate
were rebuilt from that same source/toolchain, with only the three storage/
prefill flags differing. A fresh full comparison starts after that repair.
No favorable timing was selected by excluding a measured candidate failure.

The M5 compatibility probe passes FP32 control but aborts the tested BF16
MPSMatrix combinations, as on the older host. A header enum is not runtime
support proof. This capability probe is not an inference benchmark and runs
outside all controlled timing windows.

## Correctness and storage accounting

Three native CTests pass. GPU inverse reconstruction matches **8,189,952**
finite-half/scale combinations bit-for-bit across scales −64..64. Twenty-four
native decode cases cover widths up to 9216 and real 1.7B/4B projection shapes,
generic/specialized routes, B1/B2, FP32 bits and the original FP64 envelope.
Tests also cover one-buffer accounting, half subnormals/signed zero,
unrepresentable fallback, independent contexts and abort recovery. Executed
test source is saved separately from an additional prefill extension that was
prepared later but not executed after this method failed its performance gate.

A full 4B checkpoint admission audit uploads each of 248 decoder-layer BF16
matrices individually. **247 matrices / 99.706% of their bytes** use the shared
layout; one matrix keeps the original representation. Original layer payload
is 7,138,181,120 bytes; retained matrix/scale buffers total 7,142,699,008 bytes:
**4,517,888 bytes (4.309 MiB) extra**, not a second full body copy. This is
logical per-layer buffer accounting, not whole-model peak RSS, GPU working set
or a memory saving relative to the original deployed BF16-only model. Head,
vision weights, mappings, activations and private state are excluded.

One separate fixed car-image request, 16 output tokens and capacity512,
produces matching tokens and finite states across all32 layers, but states
are **not bit-identical**. Maximum absolute state difference is
0.0001294613. The diagnostic's worst pointwise dense-coefficient ratio is
8.37; do not call it a pass of the original deep numerical suite. Changed MPS
reduction ordering prevents a bit-equivalence claim even when decoded values
and sampled text match. Full state hashes, per-part error/norm values and the
correctness-only driver are retained. Raw FP32 snapshots remain in the local
work directory; their exact hashes and reproduction inputs are preserved.

## WorldSense result

Four fresh sequential control/candidate/candidate/control processes execute
the same fixed-frame current-Skill/search-only cases and text search planning
through WorldSense → Galaxy → native Garnet. All72 complete model-call token
sequences/texts and input identities match. Model/Skill/image budgets and
chunk16 are unchanged. Warm medians use the two later repeats of every case;
all initial warmup requests remain in raw JSON. Live bindings are restored
after each suite; benchmark events and states are not committed.

| Process | 4B total p50 (s) | 4B TTFT p50 (s) | 4B decode p50 (tokens/s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| control-1 | 12.687 | 3.879 | 13.340 |
| candidate-1 | 15.589 | 3.449 | 9.694 |
| candidate-2 | 16.146 | 3.619 | 9.405 |
| control-2 | 15.116 | 5.412 | 11.878 |

4B TTFT improves11.09% and33.13%, but decode falls27.33% and20.82%; total
rises22.87% and6.81%. Text decode falls26.52% and25.33%. **Reject.** Control
drift is retained, not removed; these trials do not isolate every causal
contribution of reconstruction, scheduling, clocks or system pressure. The
original production library/profile is restored. No unchanged favorable retry
overturns the failed gate.

The earlier fixed-frame protocol's limits apply: this excludes video decode,
candidate scheduling, temporal memory, event persistence and search retrieval/
ranking. Model timings exclude loading, queues and retries. Estimated decode
uses `(tokens−1)/(total−TTFT)` and can include EOS work. Native/HTTP wall times
and VM/swap samples are separate; post-run RSS is not peak unified GPU memory.
The original full historical multi-profile numerical suite is not claimed as
a fresh M5/4B pass. All source/build identities, failures and raw observations
are retained for paper preparation rather than a general speedup claim.

# WS-M5-06: existing smaller BF16 prefill tile — rejected

Use the existing 16x32x32 tile instead of 16x64x64 only for physical rows 16. Less shared memory per threadgroup, more output tiles/input rereads, unchanged BF16 weights and FP32 values. Native reference tests and 32-layer state/token bit checks pass; actual counters prove control/candidate routing with decode untouched.

Prospectively declared single-car WorldSense/Galaxy current-event screen: both policies warm, two ABBA blocks, four measured calls per policy/model. All 20 calls match golden tokens/text/input hashes. Four-B median TTFT improves 1.42%, total 0.10%, decode decreases 0.76%; text TTFT improves 4.12%, total 2.44%. Skill native-call median 13.9603 versus 13.8613 seconds. Fails the 10% TTFT / 3% total improvement gate: rejected, no unchanged retry or full confirmation, original library/live assignments restored.

Raw calls/warmups, protocol, analysis, correctness, code/build identities and environment capture are retained. Initial preparation encoding/path failures produced no model timing. Environment timestamp is during this process, not per-call thermal telemetry. The lifecycle controller uses CPython; timed requests use XLang3 and production native WorldSense/Galaxy/Garnet. No external Python image helper. These archived-frame measurements exclude decoding/scheduling/persistence and retrieval/ranking. Single scene, small sample, one M5: no statistical or general hardware claim.

Separate fault-source/build forces second re-materialization allocation failure after first succeeds; host/private states remain unchanged, next generic call and subsequent resident calls recover exact output. Skillp50 38.1596916→38.7060935s(+1.4319%).4B TTFT+4.9454%,total+3.0431%,decode−2.1206%;textTTFT−13.8751%,total−11.1632%,decode−0.6087%. Original2%4B TTFT/total/decode-preservation gates fail. REJECT, no full confirmation/promotion/unchanged favorable retry. Logical Metal resource reduction repeats, but the favorable WS15 latency was not reproduced by this distinct implementation. Restoration verified: exact WS10 library, normal service without benchmark environment, four files online, camera unmounted, authenticated valid benchmark404.

Next distinct investigation: explicit resident graph construction that avoids the first allocation of eligible default state inputs and terminal root, with lazy ordinary-run materialization and unchanged context. Current designs allocate then retire; merely lowering reported Metal resources did not demonstrate lower task footprint here. # WS-M5-24 exact vision-weight materialization: rejected companion decode regression

WS-M5-24: Exact BF16 vision masters with reusable FP32 materialization

Status: REJECTED at independent fresh speed screen. Correctness and resource feasibility passed; companion decode throughput failed the unchanged2% preservation gate. No confirmation, promotion or unchanged retry.

Method: seed the untraced WS21 source, retaining its previously rejected measurements. Replace persistent FP32 copies of 96 BF16 block-projection weights with immutable, raw-only BF16 masters. Before each matrix use, a GPU integer kernel writes uint(ushort)<<16 into a transient FP32 buffer, zeroing row padding. The original MPS FP32 matrix multiplication remains unchanged. Distinct raw/master keys retain checkpoint metadata validation and shared owners; expanded buffers are excluded from immutable shared records. Conservative exact-layout, full-write, single-owner, hazard-tracked interval coloring permits reuse after the last consumer, protecting inputs, roots, aliases and masters. Original precision, model assets, context, pixel budget, CUDA and native image preparation are retained.

Tradeoffs: every frame adds 96 encoded expansions, reads the BF16 masters and writes FP32 workspace. Workspace pools retain their high-water allocations until graph close. The implementation initially allocates F32 shadow descriptors before pool binding, so there is no setup peak-saving claim. Header-only net payload estimate528MiB is distinct from measured whole-process results; this candidate also includes WS21 workspace/private policies.

# WS-M5-58 — Native RAW text-worker isolation rejected

## Prospective method and implementation

WS55 raw-runtime diagnosis was order-dependent; WS56/57 had exact outputs and useful resource/4B results but failed text preservation. This distinct hypothesis put the raw1.7B model in an owned native XLang3 process/context while packed4B remains in the parent. No assumption that shared context caused earlier failures.

Immutable WS54 seed, not WS56 residency or WS57 selective retirement. Default-OFF GARNET_METAL_NATIVE_TEXT_WORKER. Native C++ manager uses existing native XLang3 LRPC, checked Value.Call, same-source all-method-options-OFF child library, argument-vector posix_spawn, owned PID/birth/source/DLL checks and one global recursive serving gate. Compatible nonvisual Qwen3 metadata2048hidden/28layers determines routing; original root/xModel/cache/profile/limit arguments and all other local models retain original semantics. Parent does not load a duplicate text model. A transport error invalidates the worker; inference is not automatically retried. Explicit subsequent serve/reload is observable. Bounded stop/reap affects only owned children; native watchdog terminates the worker on actual parent death even inside native inference.

Source1723files, eight changed/new files versus1718-file WS54 seed: Metal CMake, native entry, serving clock metadata, native support header/implementation, worker manager header/implementation and native XLang3 worker script. Canonical source and historical revisions are reconstructed using the respective complete manifests and explicit overlays. No shader/codec/graph/session/xModel/FP32 math/reduction-order/model/precision/budget/CUDA/original-test changes. CUDA execution is not tested on this Mac. Shared task pages can be double-counted, so footprint is conservative, not unique physical RAM or peak usage. Device recommended working-set hint is kept once, not summed. Missing counters invalidate admission rather than becoming zero. Native two-process allocation proof established process-local Metal counters on this M5. Parent primary owner/before-after/encoded counters and raw child counters remain separately auditable; text must encode no work in the parent. All additional collection time is counted. # WS-M5-45 — Joint primary weights and resident-default retirement rejected

The candidate saved memory and improved VLM decoding, but the companion text model decoded 7.91% slower. It failed the unchanged 2% preservation gate. ## Method and source

The design predates setup and execution. The full 1715-file source closure exactly matches canonical `f21c1a2584031ee9d1c129d1e58818f9d1c826d2`, with **zero source overlay**. Only two build flags differ between OFF and ON: full-primary lossless BF16 storage and safe resident-default retirement. Both apply to both models. WS40 used primary with retirement OFF; WS15 used retirement with primary OFF; WS44 applied both only to wide VLM graphs. This is a distinct joint configuration, not a repeat of those rejected candidates or an isolated component comparison.

No shader, codec, allocation/retirement algorithm, FP32 math/K-order/reduction, Model, image preparation, serving wrapper, profile/budget, prefix policy or CUDA change. Wide-checkpoint scope, cached matrix metadata, private defaults, explicit residency sets, value16 helpers and other rejected variants are absent or OFF. Inference and image preparation use native C++/Metal/XLang3; CPython orchestrates and audits only.

The prospective weight budget was 9,033,678,080 bytes, plus existing unused-default retirement. The structural allocation projection was 16,050,486,528 bytes; actual measured Metal allocation was 16,055,271,424 bytes. The projection was not used as acceptance evidence. Native owner accounting is distinct from physical memory and driver allocation overhead.

## Correctness before timing

New OFF, ON and separate primary-fault builds exited zero. All seven native tests per build passed; all 186 complete projection records remained byte-identical at the original FP64 bounds. Both GPU primary readers checked all 398 actual packed matrices, 5,921,308,672 original FP32 words each. All 48 raw fallbacks remain; retained primary plus raw bytes match the declared budget.

Generic/resident alternation rehydrated defaults while preserving complete outputs and host/session states. Actual normal infer calls retire defaults for both ON models and never rehydrate them; OFF counters remain zero. Standalone API owners were 201 VLM and 197 text; normal jointly loaded requests used the expected combined 398-owner tuple. The old disabled lazy-fault API branch remains unexecuted and unclaimed; the original C++ primary fault checks executed.

The three original metric/golden/source analyzer ASTs remain unchanged except the declared native route predicate. Ten real correctness calls and negative capability/owner/metadata/retirement/dispatch cases passed. Complete source, checkpoint/model, library/build, frame/Skill, runtime and 1864 build/SDK/host identities were frozen before dispatch and unchanged after each stage. Hardware was additionally observed through read-only sysctl during resource execution: Mac17,4, Apple M5, 24 GiB, ten physical/logical cores. That observation is explicitly labeled after dispatch.

## Fresh WorldSense resource and speed results

Eight actual WorldSense Skill/Galaxy calls over fresh OFF/ON workers preserved complete outputs and native policy checks. Post-decode sampled maxima:

## Rejection and limits

**REJECT:** text derived decoding regressed 7.912814%, exceeding the original 2% limit. VLM decoding +20.127057%, lower latency, memory and complete Skill wall do not rescue that failure. It rejects invalid geometry/range/alignment, zero or>8Miword count and open batches before encoding. It does not change the XLang inference/image API or wrapper.

## Question and prior evidence

WS61's exact old library in a native child still had longer inner decode/GPU spans; gateway overhead alone did not explain its loss. Existing WS26 per-token timing located the loss across tokens but not individual native operations. Historical sparse counter traces targeted M4/small models and lacked explicit phases; their times are not an M5/4B baseline. Encoder reuse, concurrent projections and disjoint-grid fused projections already have rejected/mixed evidence and were not repeated unchanged.

This new diagnostic asks which custom compute-pass shapes dominate prespecified decode windows of the packed 4B/raw-text profile in real WorldSense. [Design before implementation](native-design-before-implementation.txt). It does not determine GPU clocks, bandwidth, occupancy, residency or a root cause; it does not test a new inference optimization or qualify a rejected profile for promotion.

Immutable WS54 seed has 1,718 files. Isolated source has 1,720 files/seven changed or added: Metal CMake, context header/implementation, native entry, serving metadata, new counter helper and native test. The existing XLang3 serving loop marks index+1 immediately before the unchanged decoder.step and returns the request ID. Requests restore on return/error; no scope reaches other threads, prefill/vision/status or the next request. Direct serving calls without a native request keep their original inference and remain untraced.

Only decode steps 4,16,28 are sampled. All original custom compute encoders in those commands use timestamp attachments; no new empty encoders, forced flushes, extra GPU waits or reordered dispatches. One 4,096-entry/32 KiB timestamp buffer per active context bounds each selected command to 2,048 encoder intervals. Unsupported API, capacity overflow, missing/wrong-length/zero/error/reversed timestamps and partial-command sampling fail the diagnostic instead of fabricating zero or truncating. Resolve and append/flush records after the original completed submission. FILE/descriptor/JSON/sampling work perturbs execution; this is not a serving performance build.

The native M5 capability probe found timestamp set/stage-boundary support, with dispatch/blit sampling unsupported. Two dependent passes produced all 4,096 expected values exactly and four valid raw timestamps. No checkpoint, image or model inference in that probe. See Apple's [GPU counter overview](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/gpu-counters-and-counter-sample-buffers) and [compute-pass start index](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlcomputepasssamplebufferattachmentdescriptor/startofencodersampleindex); installed SDK headers and hashes identify the compiled API.

RAW has all nine prior method flags OFF and tracing ON; PRIMARY has PRIMARY/WIDE/LAZY ON and tracing ON; packed has all nine ON and tracing ON. Quiet has the packed flags with tracing OFF. Fault has the packed/tracing flags plus test hooks. RAW/PRIMARY/packed/quiet are numerical compatibility profiles; the actual pipeline capture is candidate-only packed, as declared. There is no RAW timing comparison or speed-selection gate in this diagnostic. Existing optimization resource/speed/confirmation/canonical gates remain unchanged for a later distinct candidate.

Five builds/40 native tests passed. Review then found that the first default-OFF wrapper still evaluated label arguments; initial source/manifests/logs were preserved. Source/model/runtime/library/mathematical guard/oracle identities were hashed before learned calls and checked afterward. The outer service/test sequencing wrapper's first explicit SHA was observed after launch; its creation was recorded before launch and it stayed unchanged. That timing limitation is explicit; no prelaunch SHA record for the outer wrapper is claimed. The later actual pipeline capture froze the full outer/capture/verification driver closure before dispatch, plus all 19 assets and 1,877 compiler/build/SDK/host/backend dependencies.
